column13: body

column8: 91 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Spring rolls Sweet & sour tofu Japanese curry with rice Warm sesame milk bubble tea The bubble tea was great, but all the vegetables were badly undercooked, and the meat was really chewy.

Fish & chips This venue describes itself as an eatery, that's a bit strong. This is a bar, with a bar snacks menu, the fish in our fish & chips was fish bites. Fortunately, they allow you to order in your own Dominos. Also: karaoke.
Murray's pub burger Fish & chips The fish was a bit too fishy, the burger was dry and flavourless, although it did hold itself together well.

column8: 5 Grey Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Fried noodles, cabbage, red cabbage, red onion, carrot, garlic aioli, sweet chilli, tofu, and Singapore Steak Roast potato, cabbage, red cabbage, carrot, pickles, red onion, cheese, sesame sauce, and won tons This place is sort of like Subway, in that you choose a base (rice, potato, noodles), salads, sauces, and meats. Very popular, and frankly, we can see why. Tasty, well priced, lots of options. The potatoes were a little average, the tofu was a bit sloppy on the inside, and overall the meals were very salty, but they were very yummy. Lunch only.

column8: 44 Rangitikei Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Battered fish, chips, and salad Cheeseburger and chips What a surprise. Yes, this establishment is a bit run down and the menu is basic. But the food was well made, tasty, and excellent value for money. Exceeded expectations. In particular the salad with the fish & chips - many places just phone this salad in. Not The Royal. Fancy lettuce, red onion, carrot, cheese, capsicum, tomato, cucumber, salad dressing. Not two sad lettuce leaves and a single slice of cucumber like you get in some pubs. Also they weren't shy with the tartare and tomato sauces. And they had chicken salt on the chips for both meals, plus the burger was huge. If you want to enter the pool comp, be sure to bring your own cue. It's pretty serious business.

column8: 723 Main Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4414
column13: Chicken, cranberry, and cream cheese filo with salad Butter chicken pie with salad Carrot cake with yoghurt Banana smoothie Oh dear, everything went wrong here. Although we weren't planning on drinking anything alcoholic, this establishment loudly announces on its signage that it is a licensed cafe. Right inside the door however is a sign that says no alcohol, and this is honestly the least of their problems. There was a really long and slow queue to order, and when we did finally order two items from their menu, we were informed that the wait would be 40 minutes. That's understandable on an exceptionally busy day, but The Cooperage was only about a third full... we just ate from the cabinet. The filo, the pie, and the carrot cake were passable. The salads that came with the meals had too much dressing, too much carrot, and not a lot of anything else. There was something wrong with the yoghurt, in fact, it was inedible. Two mysterious bowls, one of sour cream and one of tomato relish were delivered, it was not exactly clear what they were supposed to accompany, so we tried them both with everything hot. That was a mistake. The smoothie was from one of those Zero Degrees powder sachets, nobody would think there was any banana involved, and there was an unpleasant aftertaste typical of these powder smoothies. The staff seemed very stressed, and on the whole, not pleased to be there. There appear to be some management issues at The Cooperage, the last time we tried to eat here we were told we could only order from the cabinet as there was no cook. The whole experience was a bummer.

column8: 327 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4414
column13: Vietnamese stir fry with fried noodles and beef Lemongrass beef vermicelli salad For a Vietnamese restaurant, you wouldn't expect so many dishes to come with chips. That said, the food was pretty nice, and came out really fast. Ambiance was a bit weird, there was a live singer who was good, but the space is just too small for her. It was like they couldn't quite decide between being a restaurant or a bar.

column8: 36 Amesbury Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: 3 cheese souffle Pumpkin risotto with stir-fried vegetables Pork belly with arancini, broccoli and pear Sticky date pudding with ice cream Nice place, intimate setting, good for couples. Very good service and meals were out really fast, complementary amuse bouche was a nice touch. The stir-fried vegetables were a poorly matched accompaniment to the risotto, which was otherwise nice. The pork belly was fantastic, mad props to the crackling. However the standout of the meal was the sticky date pudding, which is definitely the best we've had.

Vegetarian panini Ploughman's sandwich Caramel brownie slice Candy cane cheesecake Although best known for their cheesecake, Yummy Mummy's has a respectable cafe (cabinet food only). The vegetarian panini was unusual and interesting but overall very nice. It contained apple which was an eye opener, in a good way. The sandwich was fairly pedestrian but well-made and tasty. The caramel brownie slice was very caramel-y and delicious. The candy cane cheesecake was polarising - one of us found it literally inedible. The other found it rather good. Yummy Mummy's has a great range of cheesecake flavours, candy cane being a festive limited-time special.

column8: 44 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Celtic: mixed leaves, sundried tomato, cheddar, and red onion on multigrain bread Breakfast bun: bacon, egg, sausage and hollandaise on ciabatta Banana smoothie Peanut butter slab O'Briens makes a killer sandwich. The Celtic, which we asked to have without avocado, was very nice. Red onion is always a risk in a sandwich, often you get colossal pieces that all come out the side at once, in the Celtic however, the red onion was very subtle, and well proportioned. The ciabatta of the breakfast bun, was outstanding, soft, toasted to perfection, and delicious, but there were some minor structural issues. Both sandwiches came with ready salted chips, which was unusual, but not unwelcome. The banana smoothie certainly wasn't bad, but it didn't turn any heads. And the peanut butter slab was like a big Reese's piece, and what's not to like about that. It looks like a 90's Robert Harris on the inside, could use a revamp. The menu was vast and varied, truly a sandwich for every taste.

column8: 67 George Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Eggs benedict with mushroom Pork belly burger with chips Let us tell you about Steve's latte. Moxies was quite busy when we arrived, with a few reserved tables. The table next to us was reserved for Steve. While we were waiting for our meals to come out (which took 20 minutes, but they had told us 30 minutes and to be fair it was fairly busy) we watched with interest as a latte bowl complete with chocolate fish was delivered to Steve's reserved empty table for two. The latte sat there. And sat there. At a time when the latte was surely lukewarm the apparent manager (judging by the way he was bustling about and shaking hands with customers) removed the latte from the table and moved it to a neighbouring, non-reserved and much larger table. He removed the saucer and placed it atop the bowl as a lid of sorts, assumedly in a vain attempt to keep what little heat remained inside. Some time later a man and a woman arrived and sat at Steve's table. Was this Steve? Less than one minute later their meals arrived - Steve (?) and associate had clearly ordered in advance. Yet the latte remained banished to the other table. More mysteriously still, shortly after this two coffees (none of which was a latte bowl) arrived for Steve (?) and associate. Just as we were ready to give up hope, a gentleman arrived at the latte table. The manager greeted him and indicated the latte bowl, which the man started to drink. Was THIS Steve? Then who had sat at Steve's table? And why was the latte prepared SO FAR IN ADVANCE of either Steves' arrivals? We left Moxies after a pretty average meal with more questions than answers. During this drama, we did receive our food. The eggs benedict was just like a thousand others we've had. The pork belly burger was comically over-tall and so impossible to eat without deconstruction. Even if the burger hadn't been taller than Business Andy's face, pork belly is not suitable as a burger filling as it is too chewy - pulled pork would have been preferable. The burger was nice, just difficult to eat.

column8: 92 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Honey glazed beef hot plate with rice Mee goreng with BBQ pork If you want to read some classic manga, this is the place for you. If you want a nice meal, maybe you'd be better looking elsewhere. The beef was yuck, it was very chewy, and had that flavour you remember from that time you made that awful stir fry with the cheapest beef from Pak'nSave when you were first flatting. The sauce, while very sweet wasn't bad, and neither were the vegetables, but the beef ruined the whole thing. The mee goreng was reasonable, but couldn't elevate this meal above a 1 by itself.

column8: Shop 2/199 Main Street, Takaro, Palmerston North 4412
column13: Cheeseburger Chicken burger Cheesy fries Cheesecake shake Shake Out is a fast food burger establishment, with a difference. The set-up is designed to be streamlined with cashierless, cashless ordering using a tablet, a limited menu and no customisation. Speaking as people who sometimes like to remove the tomato from their burger, the lack of customisation was a little disappointing. However, the burgers were very good. Quality, fresh ingredients and great buns, these were simple burgers done well. The burgers are small which is great for lunch and was reflected in the price. The cheesy fries came with a cheese dipping sauce which was a bit heart attack-esque. The cheesecake shake was similarly artery clogging but we appreciated the unique cheesecake flavour, although it was a bit sweet and was very thick - we recommend mixing the shake thoroughly before drinking.

column8: 6 Manawaroa Street, West End, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Potato top pie Pork riblet roll Cookie caramel slice This is where your Nana would take you in the 90s, right down to the red plastic tray that slides in front of the cabinets and the teeny plates. The pastry on the potato top was extremely dry, as was as the pork riblet. The cookie caramel slice was passable.

The Pensioner Pack: fish, chips, tartare sauce Fish and cheese burger Thirty years of zero upkeep on the quintessential 80's decor has taken its toll, the result is a bit depressing. Not as depressing as the fish burger though. The burger tasted like a combination of sugar, oil, and nothing, and not in a good way. The fish in the Pensioner Pack was rubbery, although the slice of lemon was appreciated, and the chips were alright.

column8: 689 Tremaine Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4414
column13: Fish burger Satay chicken burger with chips The service in Angkor Wat was so excellent that, were there a rating for service alone, this would be at the top. The woman at the counter was an absolute delight - patient, friendly, laughed at all our jokes and even cracked one herself. Unfortunately, our rating system is not on service alone and the food at Angkor Wat was only so-so. Some care had been taken in constructing the burgers including fresh fancy lettuce and tomato. However, the fish was a little fishy and there was a bit too much lettuce in the fish burger. The satay chicken burger was a little better but still only okay. A note on the clientele. In the average population, what proportion would you expect to have a limp? Five percent? Ten percent? Try seventy-five percent (of the customers dining in, excluding us). Seems a little extreme. Did something happen here?

column8: 126 King Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Poppadums with cumin seeds Onion bhaji with tamarind sauce Paneer tikka masala with rice Beef jalfrezi with rice Aloo paratha Onion kulcha A small thing of mint yoghurt sauce Let me tell you who's punching above their weight; Tikka Talks is punching above their weight. The place looks awful. We were the only people there and decorations included a pool table, seven empty food cabinets, a childrens' play pen, a collection of four Warehouse-esque kiwi themed framed inspirational prints, and a large green dreamcatcher with a unicorn in the centre. But all this was saved by one man, and his mission, which was to upsell us at every opportunity, and to slay us with his jokes. Our original order was two curries, one plain naan, and one cheese naan, but the man drives a hard bargain, and by the time we realised that we had been worked by a skilled salesman, it was far too late. We were assured that we were going to be served something special that we were going to love, and he was right, dammit. The cumin seeds in the poppadums was a nice touch, the bhaji was just the way we like it, and the tamarind sauce, which we were proudly assured was made from scratch, was excellent. The curries themselves were both delicious. And as for the breads, the onion kulcha was sweet and tasty, while the aloo was just alright. Tikka Talks deserves more customers.

column8: 96 King Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Bacon buttie and chips Macaroni cheese If the staff at Stage Door Cafe didn't want us to eat there, they should have just said. When we arrived (at 1:30pm on a Saturday) we were the only people there and while we were told they were still cooking, their faces said otherwise. The macaroni cheese was bland although we do commend their reheating skills - reheated cabinet mac'n'cheese often comes out as a brick-like structure, but this looked like it had just been made. The bacon buttie was very disappointing. For $15 we expect more than just bread and bacon hastily slapped together. There wasn't even any sauce in the sandwich.

column8: The Grand Building, 41 The Square, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Meatlovers pizza Pesto pasta If you like huge meals, Cafe Express is the place for you. If you like nice meals, maybe not so much. The "medium" pizza and "small" pasta we ordered would have comfortably fed three people, and for a very modest price. Unfortunately, the flavours couldn't keep up with the value. The pasta was nice on the first bite. But two to three bites in it became apparent that this was really just spaghetti in a white sauce with minimal pesto and parmesan resulting in a bland dish. This became tedious very fast and was a long, long slog to the bottom of the bowl. The pizza was better than the pasta, but hardly turning heads. It was way over-cheesed. This resulted in serious structural issues as well as sogginess in the centre of the pizza. The meats themselves were fine, but the pizza could have done with a BBQ sauce or something to add a little pizzazz. Also, there was a cat tower near the kitchen. Tragically we never saw any cats.

Eye fillet, polenta chips and BBQ sauce Beef burger with chips Rustic Steak House does simple food, but does it pretty well. The burger was basic but tasty. Particularly welcome was the steak knife through the middle of the burger, allowing the burger to be cut in half making it a breeze to eat. The eye fillet was properly cooked and came with the very welcome surprise of a half clove of roasted garlic. A little side salad wouldn't have gone amiss.

Fish & Chips Fisherman's Basket If we were rating for atmosphere alone, Cloverlea Tavern would be a 4. Sensational karaoke, everyone knew everyone, there was a meat raffle going around, and we spotted the world's most magnificent mullet crooning "Country Roads." However, Business Andy & the Fee-Rex is a restaurant review blog, not a bar atmosphere review blog. The menu was bar snacks, but some effort had been made. There was a tasty seasoning on top and both tartare and tomato sauce on the side. The fish was just fish bites, but they were about as good as fish bites get. The shrimp and squid rings were good, however the mussels were a bit old. Maybe it was the karaoke, or maybe it was the mullet, in any case we were strongly reminded of our time at Castle 789. For the record, Cloverlea Tavern is better in every way.

Macaroni cheese Nachos Banana smoothie Cafe Ignition has a great view. Of the tarmac. This is the cafe at the Palmerston North airport. And you can tell they're used to a captive clientele. The food was bland across the board. The smoothie was the highlight. The lowlight was the macaroni cheese. We saw the individually served bowls in the cabinet, with a garnish of two slices of tomato, a couple of spinach leaves and a sprinkling of red onion on top. When this was served to us, the garnish was steaming hot. They had clearly just chucked the whole thing in the microwave. How lazy is that?! Considering there were no flights for the next 3 hours and the place was nearly completely empty, they had plenty of time to remove the garnish prior to heating if they had cared enough to do so. Speaking of things they didn't care to do, perhaps the staff could do less sitting-in-the-corner-doing-a-crossword-puzzle and more wiping of tables and chairs, which were crumb-fest 2021. If you do, for some reason, still want to go to this cafe, then a note on parking. Unless you want to pay exorbitant airport parking fees, you will need to park some ways away. And we recommend you do not pay for airport parking, as you will need all your money to pay the ripoff airport prices for your tasteless meal.

Beef bao buns Beef burger and chips They say that in 2021, $25 won't get you much for dinner. The person who said that has never been to The Empire; the value for money here is immense. The beef bao buns were tasty, although the beef was a little chewy. And the beef burger was similarly tasty, with a patty that was a bit on the dry side. The burger also fell apart spectacularly, and the Fee-Rex was covered in a sticky mixture of caramelised onion and tomato after just a few mouthfuls. It's already been said, but needs to be said again, the value for money here is spectacular. This humungous and delicious meal was the same price as the miserable lunch we had at the Stage Door Cafe recently. How do they do it? What are their secrets?

We ate lunch here in February 2021 Margherita melt BBQ melt Warning: melt means large pizza bread. Two of these was way too much for us, one would have been about right. That said, they were both quite nice. There was plenty of mozzarella on the Margherita melt, and having cherry tomatoes instead of slices of regular tomatoes was the way to go. The BBQ melt was very meaty and hearty, and had plenty of sauce; a winning combo. On your arrival at Orlando Country Club, you'll notice the large sign detailing the dress code. No stubbies, no singlets, no hoodies, and presumably no facial tats. Who do they think they are? This isn't a real country club, it's just a driving range and cafe. And by the way, we saw all of these rules violated while we were there. Website

We ate dinner here in February 2021 Meatball sub on rye bread (non-toasted) with smoked cheese, spinach, cucumber, onion, carrot, capsicum, olives, garlic aioli, and pepper Steak panini with mozzarella, spinach, onion, capsicum, honey mustard, and ranch dressing When you order a steak panini at Subway, you're not expecting eye fillet, but you're also not expecting dry steak with a layer on top that we genuinely thought was mushroom, but on reflection, was probably fat. This panini was flavourless, and we know what you're thinking, Subway is what you make it. However on this occasion, we used the Subway recommended salads and cheese, and got a very bland result. Our compliment for this panini is that it was piping hot, some cafes could learn a lesson from Subway here. Fortunately, the meatball sub was a bit better, but ultimately only reaches the level of "adequate." Why would you eat at Subway when O'Briens Irish Sandwich Cafe exists? Website

We ate dinner here in February 2021 Lamb madras with rice Paneer lababdar with rice Plain naan Cheese & garlic naan Hey 4Flames, turn down the damn air conditioning. You know there's a real problem when you can hear people at other tables also complaining about being cold. We felt bad for the women who showed up wearing tiny skirts as we were leaving. Putting the enthusiastic temperature regulation aside, the curries were very nice and quite different. The lababdar was sweet and creamy, and the madras was coconutty. Unfortunately, the chunks of paneer and lamb were far too big, and the paneer was very dense. The lamb was good for curry-grade lamb, but it was still curry-grade lamb. The presentation of the curries was atypical, and we liked it. Gone were the typical cauldrons of curry sauce with submerged chunks and the plate for mixing. Instead it was like how you make a curry at home; all in a bowl. This was way better, with the opportunity to just add rice to your bowl and mix - voila! If you're looking for a quick meal, we recommend avoiding Friday night dining as the takeaway side of the business was pumping and dine-in wait times suffered. Reservations are strongly recommended. Website

We ate lunch here in February 2021 Creamy mushrooms on toast Big breakfast: bacon, sausage, eggs, toast, hash browns, mushrooms Banana smoothie When we arrived at Trio Cafe, we were alone, and the waitress looked surprised to see us. The whole time we were there, we were alone. When we ordered, she had to look up all the prices, we suspected that we were their first customers ever. We thought "this doesn't look good." When the smoothie arrived, and was really a banana milkshake with a banana blended in, unmixed banana syrup at the bottom, a swirl of canned whipped cream on the top, and a flimsy straw that was far too small we thought, "this really doesn't look good." But then the food arrived, and the whole thing turned around. The mushrooms on toast were outstanding, and that's not an easy thing to say about mushrooms on toast which are often mundane. The bread was delicious sourdough. The mushrooms themselves were so flavourful, we don't even know how they did it. They came with a game-changing smear of pesto and a little balsamic reduction on the side which left us wondering why we aren't all eating our mushrooms this way. The big breakfast hadn't phoned it in. Herbed focaccia for the toast, the steaky bacon: perfectly crisped, two hash browns, mushrooms (unfortunately, not the same as on the other plate), and a cheesy sausage they had innovated split down the middle and cooked as two separate halves that had curled deliciously. It was even decoratively garnished with balsamic reduction and julienne vegetables. Our only complaint was slightly underdone eggs, which were supposed to come "your way" as per the menu, except they never asked and just came fried. Website

Man burger with chips Fish, chips, and salad The Ashhurst Inn has a very special place in our hearts. As Ashhurst residents, we are keen to support what is literally the only dine-in dinner establishment in the whole village, plus the Inn was the site of a very early date for Business Andy and The Fee-Rex. It pains us to say that this meal was bad, but it was bad, especially the burger. In fact, the man burger was tragic, it looked like the kind of disappointing burger that you make at home. While you're making it, you're so certain that it's going to be great, but then you realise that the patty is so dry that it's crumbling, the bun has been toasted way too long, there's not nearly enough sauce, the cheese isn't melted, you haven't put enough bacon in it, and the hash brown doesn't save it. The fish and chips wasn't as bad as the burger, with both key components being passable. The salad, however, was a disgrace. Every ingredient was flavourless and tossed in a gross oily sauce. Shout out to the homemade tartare sauce, although it's sad when the best part of two meals is tartare sauce. Website

We ate dinner here in March 2021 Rodeo burger regular combo with a banana shake Streaky bacon steakhouse regular combo with L&P We knew we were off to a bad start when we arrived and saw seven (7!) people waiting for their food. Some of them probably had their food already, but had frozen solid and were unable to leave. We can only assume The King turns the temperature down that low to discourage youths from loitering in his fine establishment on a Friday night. Although they asked if we would be dining in at their wobbly, sticky tables, they still just gave us our meal in a takeaway bag anyway, making us feel even more unwelcome. To make matters worse, the food was awful. If the Burger King was alive to eat these burgers, he would have rolled over in his grave. For both burgers, the sauce did a lot of heavy lifting, attempting to moisten each mouthful and also disguise the other flavours. The rodeo burger was a little better than the streaky bacon steakhouse, which was a bit sad considering that the steakhouse burger is supposed to be from their premium range. It was anything but. The bun was stale, the distribution of ingredients was patchy, and when you got a taste of the meat without sauce, you wished that you hadn't. The chips were hot and fresh at least, but both drinks were bad in their own ways. The L&P was watery, and the banana shake tasted like depleted uranium. Business Andy actually used to work at a Burger King a long time ago, and this was every bit as bad as he remembers. Website

column8: 361 Broadway Avenue, Terrace End, Roslyn, Palmerston North 4414
column13: Rating: 1 We ate lunch here in March 2021 Sweet chilli chicken calzone Vegetarian stuffed potato Banana smoothie Coffee on the Terrace advertises that they are open until 2:30pm on a Saturday. So you can colour us surprised when we arrived at 1:10 to find the kitchen closed, and a member of staff bringing in the sign from the footpath. Luckily, cabinet food was still available. Unluckily, we ordered the calzone. Jesus it was bad, bready, dry, and flavourless. It wasn't even really a calzone, do they even know what a calzone is? The potato was far better, but it's hard not to be. The vegetables other than potato were nondescript. If you were wearing a blindfold while eating this and were asked what vegetables were in there, your answer would have been just potato. At least it was hot all the way through. The banana smoothie obviously had some banana syrup in it as well as a real banana. Not awful but not good either. Website

We ate lunch here in March 2021 Banana smoothie Cheese and pineapple toasted sandwich Beef burger with chips A good toastie is a thing of true beauty, however too many cafes have the toasted sandwich as a throwaway, easy addition to the menu for no other reason other than because they have the ingredients. Long Black Cafe falls into this category. They had at least done a grainy bread instead of a plain white sandwich loaf, but there was very little love put into this toastie. We're not saying this to single out Long Black Cafe, most toasties are like this, this frustration has been building for a while, and it's time to cry shame on anyone who does this to the toastie sandwich. Crushed pineapple should not be used in a toasted sandwich, it's too wet and it gives you a soggy inner bread surface. This toastie did have a good amount of cheese, and at least they cut it into triangles and not the dreaded and baleful rectangular slice. Our recommendation to cafes everywhere is to just not offer a toasted sandwich if you are going to treat it with this much contemptuous disrespect. The smoothie had quite a bit going for it, excellent texture and temperature, with a wide metal straw, it could have been a bit sweeter though. The burger was a let down for $20 in Woodville. These guys need to head down the road to Empire Sports Empire Sports & Garden Bar Restaurant to check out a burger that is 25% cheaper and 250% better. The bun was plain, the patty was of the dig-out-of-a-freezer-for-a-quick-Sunday-dinner variety, and the cheese was plastic. The salad in it was actually quite nice, and they had put it on the bottom bun, which is the proper way to construct a burger. Unfortunately, they decided to lubricate the patty on both sides with the melted sheet of plastic cheese on top and thick slices of slippery tomato on the bottom. As if to warn us of the trap that had been laid, the lid of the burger dismounted from the rest of it as the plate was put on our table. Website Please note the sign on the building says Long Black Cafe, but the website and menu both say Cafe 88

We ate lunch here in March 2021 Beef nachos Roast vege filo with salad Liquorice allsort slice Focal Point Cafe is tidy and good looking, probably due to being less than a year old. Unless it's a hot day we recommend you do not sit near the door, which is the automatic sliding variety that opened and closed constantly letting in blasts of cold wind. Credit to Focal Point for serving something we'd never seen in a cafe cabinet before, the liquorice allsort slice. While this was very sweet, it was also yum and had a good sense of fun to it. The filo was good too, and while the salad initially seemed overdressed the dressing was very tasty so this was a welcome surprise. The nachos were unfortunate. The ratios were well off, with too much bland mince for the number of chips. The cheese was a solid layer on top making it impossible to dunk the nachos into the mince mixture. And it didn't even come with any cutlery, so clearly they were expecting us to eat hot fistfuls of mince with our bare hands once all the nachos were gone. Website

column8: 700 Main Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4414
column13: We ate dinner here in March 2021 Sweet and sour pork Lemon chicken Rice Tasty Restaurant has a very authentic looking menu, but tonight we chose to go with a couple of honky classics which are generally a safe bet. We were wrong. The lemon chicken was ferociously sweet and yellow, and definitely void of any actual lemons. Rather than doing pieces of fried chicken, they'd gone for the vastly inferior giant slabs of chicken deep fried, then sliced, with sauce poured all over. The sweet and sour pork was a little better, at least they did little pieces of pork instead of half a pig sliced up. The pineapple was tasteless and the sauce has this unpleasant tang. Maybe we'd have been better off ordering the spicy duck blood with omasum instead of trying to play it safe. Website

column8: Shop 3/754 Manukau Road, Royal Oak, Auckland 1023
column13: We ate lunch here in March 2021 Bacon backfire burger: grilled chicken, brie, bacon, lettuce, red onion, tomato Low rider burger: crispy fried chicken, caramelised onion, cheese, lettuce, red onion, tomato There's not much to say about Burgerfuel. It's among the better burger places, we certainly would choose it over Burger King, no disrespect to the King himself. The burgers were both flavourful and well constructed, although both came with tomato after we asked for none. Shout out to the Doofer, it must be aggressively trademarked otherwise everyone would be copying it. Website

We ate dinner here in March 2021 Massaman curry with braised beef Lemon honey stir fry with crispy fried fish Rice Roti Sigh. This meal was bad. The cocktails came first, and they were sickly. They were too sweet even for the Fee-Rex, and that's saying something. Next came the fish, no other dishes appeared. The fish was not delish. The fillets themselves appeared to be cheap crumbed hoki pieces from the nearby New World's frozen section. Also from the frozen section was Home Brand mixed vegetable, carrot, corn, and peas topped up with a some unwelcome tomato and additional carrot. The only good bit was the pineapple where they had rightly used big chunks instead of little pieces. There was such a lengthy wait before anything else showed up that we had almost finished the fish, not that we wanted to. Then came the massaman curry, which didn't taste like much other than sugar and almost comically dry beef. We were at least looking forward to the roti which we were hoping would be a reliable option. But somehow they even managed to ruin roti. It was unevenly cooked, tasted like it had been found under a couch, and they had even failed to cut it all the way through. If for some reason you want to visit Thai Chef's Restaurant, bookings are highly recommended because they were inexplicably packed. Website

column8: 120 Hereford Street, Christchurch Central City, Christchurch 8011
column13: We ate lunch here in April 2021 1/4 lb beef burger regular meal Chicken pretzel pub burger This meal was a real mix of fresh highs and cheesy lows. The beef burger was very good, fresh ingredients, and a great ratio of bun:salad:sauce:meat. The fries were fresh, crispy, thicccccc, and neither over nor under salted. They had a pump your own sauce station, which was a great throwback to the 90's, and the L&P was not watered down. The chicken burger was a tragedy. The culprit: a foul beer cheese sauce, which tasted like neither beer nor cheese. The burger was sopping with it, completely obscuring all other flavours. It is hard to believe that anybody would enjoy that sauce, and nobody would enjoy that quantity of it. The pretzel pub range is for a limited time only, thankfully. Website

We ate dinner here in April 2021 Nachos with beef mince Fish, chips, & salad The Cheltenham Hotel (the Chelty, as it is affectionately known by its loyal clientele) is a warm and inviting country pub, complete with a border collie sleeping on an old three piece suite, locals who get their own drinks, and a handle club that meets every Thursday. The food was okay to okay+. The nachos were a bit bland, however they were crisp all the way down, finally someone worked out that you shouldn't be making them all soggy by dumping mince on top. In a surprise twist, the fish was panko crumbed but was unfortunately a bit fishy and processed. The chips were crisp with a tasty herbed salt, and the salad showed some effort had been made, including the addition of a cherry tomato and a slice of beetroot. Website

We ate lunch here in April 2021 Lamb iskender with satay sauce, hummus, and garlic aioli Falafel and eggplant doner with mild chilli sauce and garlic yoghurt We appear to have walked into a couple breaking up. The waitress and the cook at Gold Kebabs didn't exchange a single word the whole time we were there. Their awkwardness permeated through the whole restaurant and we were pleased to leave. Fortunately the iskender was good, unfortunately the doner wasn't. Apart from the frigid atmosphere and the odd little leather pouch that the cutlery came in, this was pretty standard Turkish fare. Gold Kebabs have no website or Facebook, but here is a Restaurant Guru listing.

We ate dinner here in April 2021 Beef ishtew Paneer butter masala Rice Plain naan Indian Love Story is blingin'. Chandeliers, gold trim on everything, glitter in the red and gold textured wallpaper, sparkling glittery storage boxes covering one wall. The waitress may have been blinded by this, as she didn't seem to notice things like us waiting to order, or plates sitting on tables. We are being a little unfair here, as there was clearly too much work for a single waitress. Both curries were very sweet. While the paneer butter masala did say 'sweet' in the description, this was above and beyond. The sugar hit in the ishtew was dominant, unexpected and unwelcome. The beef was chewy, stringy and overdone in that unfortunate way we've all had from curries before. The paneer was nice, as were the naans. Website

We ate lunch here in April 2021 Smorgasbord: pork wontons, steamed brocolli, vegetarian spring rolls, vegetarian samosas, fried noodles, sweet & sour pork, black bean pork, egg foo yong, prawn crackers If you find yourself needing to eat at The Plaza food court, we do not recommend Red Lantern. The steamed broccoli was the only item that wasn't bad, and this was probably only because we saw them bring it out fresh in front of us. The low points were numerous and deep, with joint honours going to the spring rolls and the fried noodles, which were cold. Just because you are a food court Chinese smorgasbord does not excuse the blatant lack of effort and care shown at Red Lantern. If you choose to subject yourself to Red Lantern, make sure you order a drink or you will suffer the icy cold displeasure of the counter staff. Red Lantern does not have a website but here is their listing in The Plaza directory

We ate dinner here in April 2021 Vegetarian pad thai Red curry roast duck with rice and roti Bangkok Thai is very ordinary. The most notable features were the giant pink plush hippo lounging at one of the tables, and the larger than average serve of roti. This is a short review, the food was acceptable. Website

We ate lunch here in May 2021 Butter chicken with rice and garlic naan Mango chicken with rice and plain naan Shamiana serves quintessential food court Indian food. All your favourites were there, including the combo for a curry, rice, naan and can of coke. Dishes were mild and very sweet. The naans were fresh, which is not a given at the food court. However, given the way Shamiana were stacking the naans high and not rotating them, our naan freshness was more luck than good food management. Tables were at a premium, or at least they were at lunchtime on a Saturday. This holds for any Plaza food court establishments, and is not specifically a concern at Shamiana. There was not quite enough of the mango sauce for the portion of rice provided. They only had one bowl left when we got there, so the butter chicken came in a takeaway container which was slightly larger and there was enough of that sauce. So giving out enough sauce to properly saturate your rice isn't an issue, they just choose not to do it. Shamiana does not have a website but here is their listing in The Plaza directory

We ate dinner here in May 2021 Apple and mint arancini with salad and tandoori mayo Fettuccine with sundried tomato and spinach Lamb shank with potato mash and green beans Essence was delightfully unpolished, it's a little bit fancy but not quite pulling it off in an endearing way. The menu was actually quite good, they push the boat out a little and have a few really interesting dishes, but they stop short of really pushing the envelope. They know that some Feilding locals want to have something a bit special, but others just want to have a burger. The arancini stood out with a unique flavour combination which worked really well. This was on their specials menu but it was so good that it should be a full time offering. The fettuccine was nice but had too much onion. And the shank was a little dry but came with a delicious jus. Website

column8: 21 Rangitikei Street, City Center, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate dinner here in May 2021 Lamb moussaka with salad, rice, and Turkish bread Chicken breast stuffed with mushroom, topped with bÃ©chamel sauce with salad, rice, and Turkish bread We'll start with the things that we could agree on. It was odd that both meals, although they appeared different in the menu, were almost identical. Two thirds of each plate was exactly the same. The rice was nice. And overall, the joint was a bit cold, with a nearby door letting in frequent icy blasts. We were divided on the rest. Review 1: When it first came over, I had a strong whiff of French toast. I've never had that before when someone brought over my evening meal, and I really thought someone nearby was having breakfast for dinner. The sauce was the source of the odour. For some reason the bÃ©chamel was unnaturally sweet and nutmeg-ey. On top of ruining the chicken, I was displeased to find that the sauce had contaminated other elements of the meal. The salad itself was acceptable, classic, Turkish style salad, like what I'd expect to get with an iskender. While not offensive in and of itself, it was bizarre to combine with the stuffed chicken breast. I don't have such a strong opinion about the moussaka. The lamb was fine, however the veggies were an indistinguishable mush. Review 2: I thought the chicken was an unusual thing to pair with your classic Turkish salads. Particularly incongruous was the raw cucumber next to a hot stuffed chicken breast. However once the cucumber and tomato were out of the way, the salad turned out to be great. The chicken breast was pretty nice, and the sauce really didn't deserve to get ripped a new one like it just did in the other review. The salad and co. paired very well with the moussaka which was absolutely delicious. It was savoury and hearty, and was just what the doctor ordered on a chilly night. Honestly I could have eaten that moussaka all over again as soon as I'd finished. Website

Rating: 1 We ate lunch here in May 2021 Corn fritters with bacon and egg added Vegetable stack What is up with the popularity of Columbus Coffee? This chain of mediocre cafes has been around for more than 25 years, and they are everywhere. We have two in Palmerston North alone, and this particular cafe was doing a steady trade. This makes no sense, as the food here is on the bad side of middle-of-the-road, and the prices are exorbitant. We paid more than $50 for two meals and one ginger beer. That almost buys a house in Palmerston North! Worst of all, the menu is littered with predatory recommendations for add-ons. We foolishly decided to take these up, adding bacon and egg to the corn fritters. No price for the add-ons is obvious in the menu. We were shocked to find that they were charging $5 for two sad pieces of bacon, and $4.50 for a single egg. Why would anybody eat here when you could have better food for cheaper at Trio Cafe? The vegetable stack featured a very dry pumpkin rosti, under-cooked haloumi, and some "salsa" that was mostly corn kernels and looked absolutely nothing like the picture in the menu. The fritters were doughy, heavy on the fritter and light on the corn. Website

column8: 109 Devon Street East, New Plymouth Central, New Plymouth 4310
column13: We ate dinner here in May 2021 Buffet-style meals We were really looking forward to a walk down memory lane at Gengy's. Last time either of us ate here we were both starving students trying to eat all we could and walk out with spring rolls in our pockets. The prices today reflect this proud history. It's a bargain if you absolutely stuff your face, but for the more restrained diner, or really for anyone who doesn't want to pop like Mr Creosote, the pricing is a bit on the steep side. We estimate $25 at most would be a fair price for what we ate, Gengy's charges $33.99, not $34.00, but just one easy payment of $33.99. For this low, low price, you get to enjoy a buffet style meal with a twist. On top of a standard buffet featuring cold fish bites, cold onion rings, cold spring rolls, and cold chicken nuggets, you can fill a bowl with your choice of raw meat, vegetables, oil, and sauce to be cooked while you wait on a giant ring shaped hot plate. The meat was was as cheap and nasty as it comes, with all the gristle to match but they did have a good variety of fresh vegetables. They had plenty of sauces, oils, and topping bits, allowing many different flavour combinations. But wait, there's more. All-you-can-eat, made-to-order pancakes, plus a dessert bar with cheap ice cream, five sauces, sprinkles, nuts, jelly, fruit, whipped cream, and butter. Top tip: Gengy suggests having peanuts or butter or maple flavoured sauce on a pancake, we discovered that all three together is absolutely delicious. Even though the food isn't particularly good, that's not why you eat here, it's fun to eat at Gengy's. Bookings recommended. Website

We ate lunch here in May 2021 Macaroni cheese Beef nachos Banana smoothie The Bees Knees has a real fussy old lady vibe. Not a surface is wasted, with old fashioned teacups cluttered amongst preserves, packaged homemade biscuits and greeting cards for sale. This is a small cafe with tiny tables crammed close together, it's honestly a bit claustrophobic. The food was a disappointment. The macaroni cheese was incredibly bland, consisting only of a basic white sauce with macaroni in it and cheese on top. Perhaps their kitchen was too cluttered with granny junk for them to locate their salt, pepper, mustard, paprika, or anything else that might have made this meal not taste like pasty nothing. The nachos were no better, with watery mince and not enough cheese. The meals were small, which we were grateful of given the taste. They were at least affordably priced. In a surprising twist, the banana smoothie was the best we've had in some time. Website

column8: 22 George Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate dinner here in May 2021 Malai kofta Paneer makhani Plain naan Cheese & garlic naan We're just going to say it, one of these curries wasn't a curry at all. The paneer makhani was clearly a can of tomato soup mixed with sugar and some leftover butter chicken sauce. It was very thin and the paneer was rubbery, dry, and highly cuboid; clearly store bought. It was at least cheap, but cheap food doesn't have to suck. The malai kofta was a bit better, and they didn't skimp on the koftas either. In addition to cooking some pretty questionable curries, Indian2nite also tried to hoodwink us in the naan department. Cheddar is a pretty flavourful variety of cheese, and if you replace it with something else, people are going to notice. Don't bait us with cheddar cheese in the menu, then switch out the cheese in the naan with stringy and flavourless mozzarella. The nerve. The plain naan was as advertised at least, plain and serviceable. Website

We ate lunch here in May 2021 Beef nachos Hash stack Banana smoothie Cafe 116 is better than their old-fashioned, designed-on-Windows-Publisher-'95 signage would suggest. We drive past this place regularly and always figured it was a real dive. It is tucked away next to a dirt bike & jetski shop and just looks a bit sad from the outside. So you can colour us surprised to find that the inside was large and airy with high ceilings and a cosy fire burning. The menu was standard cafe fare, but done relatively well. The nachos had made some effort to double-layer their cheese (cheese on top plus a second layer of melted cheese half way down) which was appreciated. The mince was on the flavourless side but there was plenty of sour cream. The menu did state "smashed avocado" on top of the nachos, when actually there were just two small avocado slices. The hash brown stack was tasty, with the right ratios of hash to bacon to mushroom plus a perfectly cooked egg and some welcome pesto and balsamic. The banana smoothie caused some debate, with Business Andy making the accusation that it contained banana syrup (as well as real banana), while the Fee-Rex was not so sure. Flavouring issues aside, the smoothie had the correct texture and coldness. Website

column8: 4 Coleman Place, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate dinner here in May 2021 Singapore steak Vegetarian laksa In many ways, Angkor is quite unremarkable. But it is remarkably popular, in fact, we've been turned away without a reservation more than once. The Singapore steak was very large, very sweet, and the large pieces of meat were mostly good quality with just a few chewy bits. The laksa was richly flavoured, and like the Singapore steak was a large meal. Speaking of large, the vegetables in the laksa were very large, and frankly it was a problem. Not only was no knife provided, but the cutting surface was a bowl of soup, even if a knife had been provided, it still would have been difficult. Don't only partially cut up the vegetables into pieces that have to be bitten off a fork in several mouthfuls. Bookings essential. Website

column8: Kabbaba, Food Court, Plaza Shopping Centre, 84 The Square, Manawatu, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate lunch here in May 2021 Lamb iskender with sweet chilli, hummus, and mayonnaise Lamb doner with hot chilli, satay, and yoghurt How dare you charge extra for satay sauce and garlic aioli? These are standard kebab sauces and should carry no extra charge over any of the other sauces. News flash, garlic aioli is basically just mayo. Maybe this was the source of the three customer complaints that we witnessed in the short time we were there, or maybe it was the absurdly long wait between ordering and eating. To be fair, the Plaza was positively heaving with people on the day we were there, so they were perhaps a lot busier than they expected. The food itself was acceptable. The doner was just the right size to actually fit in your mouth, and consequently was the right size for lunch. In contrast, the iskender was enormous, no Turkish bread came with it though. So aside from the busy food court setting, the angry customers, and the expensive sauces, Kabbaba just blends into the background hum of every other ordinary Turkish establishment. Website

We ate dinner here in June 2021 Lamb pot pie with garlic bread "Mor burger" (double beef) with chips Rosie O'Grady's is a typical Irish pub, cosy fires, walls covered in Irish paraphernalia, Guinness on tap, and offering typical Irish pub fare. The meals were basic but done well. The pot pie was very hearty, no gristly bits or unpleasant surprises in the stew with a crispy pastry top and nice thin garlic bread. The burger was pretty full on, with two large patties and was too big to be eaten with hands. It came with a couple of homemade beer battered onion rings that were much appreciated. Website

column8: 84 Fitzherbert Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We at lunch here in June 2021 BBQ pork pancake Beef & cheese bao bun Eugh. This meal sucked, and they messed up our order to boot. The bao bun was the most offensive. The bun itself was doughy and sweet, the "cheese" was in fact a cheese sauce that didn't resemble cheese in any way, and the beef was as chewy and dry as an old boot. The pancake was like a kebab, with a thin and delicate egg pancake on the outside instead of a wrap, however the pancake tore and spilled its contents everywhere. It didn't help that it was wrapped haphazardly in baking paper, just tearing a bit of the paper off caused the thin pancake to practically disintegrate. There's a Turkish joint not three doors down where they have solved this issue, the answer is foil. The filling was alright, with some crispy bits of pork crackling thrown in to add an interesting texture, however it was intensely salty. We barely finished this meal, looking down at the last bite of the bao bun was like looking into the black abyss of your own mortality. Website

We ate dinner here in June 2021 Chicken burger and chips Grilled vegetable and haloumi stack Jimmy Cook's has fallen into the classic hotel restaurant trap of thinking that if you put truffle oil in a couple of things and charge like a wounded bull, then you're automatically a fancy joint. In reality, the decor was dated, the furniture cheap, the service clumsy, and the food decidedly meh. Our waiter was personable and friendly, our orders were taken promptly, and food came out fast. However, they also forgot to bring us a wine list, and when we asked our waiter what vegetables came in the stack he was clearly guessing, and only got one guess out of three right. Two if you count haloumi as a vegetable. Speaking of the vegetable stack, this was a horrendous rip off. The meal was tiny, which wasn't a problem in and of itself, and we were warned that it was a small meal, but $25 for a sad and minuscule grilled veggie salad featuring some haloumi is outrageous. This was in no way a stack, the highest point was about 3cm off the plate, it looked like it had fallen over. It did taste okay at least. In contrast, the burger was huge, yet inexplicably was listed alongside the haloumi "stack" as a small meal. It was notably missing the beer battered onion rings that were mentioned in the menu, however we're not really that upset that they didn't show up as the table next door had what was clearly crumbed onion rings with their chicken burger. The type that comes with no guarantee of actual onion on the inside. They had also done a sneaky switcheroo on the advertised tomato sauce which was very obviously BBQ sauce. The burger itself was merely okay, the ingredients were cheap and not particularly well prepared. A note on reservations. When we first tried to eat at Jimmy Cook's we were turned away as they were fully booked. This would normally mean we advise booking, however trying to book dinner at Jimmy Cook's involved so much waiting on the phone and so many transfers that we can hardly recommend it. Just show up and try your luck, and if they are full, then that's probably for the best anyway.

column8: 54 George Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate lunch here in June 2021 Cheese scone with avocado, cream cheese, and relish Pastrami bagel with alfalfa sprouts, cheese, and cream cheese Apple and ginger muffin Decaf Americano Cyclista is an espresso bar first and an eatery a distant second. The food selection is minimal and limited to a few baked goods and whatever can be prepared in a microwave or toaster. The fact that there was just one guy rostered on a Saturday for the lunch rush is further evidence that they don't plan to sell a lot of food. That said, neither our food nor our coffee took long to arrive, so props to that one guy. The scone was fairly flavourless, but inoffensive otherwise and the pastrami bagel was okay. The muffin was too dense and too wet, as can happen with apple muffins. The coffee was pretty good, it's really why you'd go to Cyclista in the first place. Website

column8: 2202 Centre St NE, Calgary, AB T2E 2T5, Canada
column13: We ate dinner here in June 2021 Lamb satay with rice cubes Beef rendang curry with rice and salad Prediction: Lina's will close by the end of the year. This place is awful, and the lamb satay is one of the worst meals that we've reviewed. The ambiance was depressing. Everything was very obviously cheap, there were four different kinds of chairs in the restaurant, some of which inexplicably still had the plastic on them. The ambient music was a tinny radio in the kitchen, the plants were all plastic, and the place was echoingly deserted. Despite being open for a couple of months, the drinks fridge was completely empty, and drinks were not mentioned by our waitress at all. The beef rendang curry that showed up was very different to the beef rendang curry that we were expecting, it was pretty much just slow cooked beef in meat juice. That said, it was actually okay, the salad on the side was clearly a bit of an afterthought, but this meal was head and shoulders above the satay. The satay was listed as a "Chef's Special" in the menu. We fail to see what is so special about skewers of extremely chewy lamb accompanied by a watery-with-chunks peanut sauce and giant bits of raw red onion. We suppose that you could call the rice cubes "special," we've certainly never had anything like it before. It was cold (fridge cold, not room temperature cold) gelatinous roughly cut blocks of rice. And it was disgusting. We were pretty bummed out by the time we finished, but Lina still had one more surprise up her sleeve. As we were wiping our faces, desperate to ensure that we didn't leave any satay residue for later, we noticed the serviettes were branded. With Anyavee, the last restaurant that died here. At this rate the next restaurant to occupy this cursed address will probably still have some of Anyavee's serviettes leftover to use. Lina's has no website

column8: 325 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4414
column13: Rating: 1 We ate lunch here in June 2021 Fish and chips Hash brown breakfast LA Bakery is a throwback to a time when almost everything had to come with chips. Lots of chips, and a fried egg on top. Both meals were huge and cheap. The hash brown breakfast involved hash browns, a massive deep fried sausage, streaky bacon, and two pieces of dollar loaf with a fried egg on each. A lot of food for $14.90, cost of ingredients: $4.10 by our estimation. The fish was so bad that we, card carrying members of the clean plates club, left more than half of it behind. It was probably caught some time last year, and had been battered in house by someone who had only heard a rough description of what battering was. The batter had split open in the cooking process exposing the fish directly to the oil with predictable results. Inedible. LA Bakery & Coffee Lounge has no website.

column8: 140 Fitzherbert Avenue, West End, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate dinner here in June 2021 Pulled duck burger with poutine Mongolian beef salad Holy duck, what a burger. It was extremely juicy, flavourful, and unusual. We didn't expect a middling hotel restaurant to push the boat out like this. The poutine was delicious, and it was so nice to have something that wasn't just chips and tomato sauce on the side. The salad was boring and frankly there was nothing Mongolian about it. It's a pity that the salad couldn't keep up with the burger, La Patio's rating was really dragged down by some dead Mongolian weight. When you visit La Patio, be sure to keep an ear out for their instrumental cover tracks, which ranged from Radiohead to Shawn Mendes, to The Beatles. Guessing what song was being covered was a fun challenge, not to brag, but we got them all except one.

column8: 163 The Square, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate dinner here in June 2021 Centaur pizza Beef & bÃ©arnaise pizza Pompeii Pizza was a bit disappointing. The pizza bases had a store bought feel, even if they weren't. And on the whole, the ingredients were a bit bland and low quality. The beef on the beef and bÃ©arnaise pizza was the worst offender, it was as chewy as an old tyre, but the rest of the pizza wasn't much better. And it wouldn't kill you to cut up your tomatoes, nobody wants a slice of tomato that covers half the pizza. The centaur pizza might as well have been just a beetroot and balsalmic pizza because that's all you could actually taste. You could see the feta and you could feel the texture of the walnuts, but otherwise, they were undetectable. Website

We ate lunch here in June 2021 Keto toasted sandwich Polenta, haloumi, and vegetable stack Carrot cake Banana smoothie Mocha This is not the Robert Harris that you remember from 90's trips to get a pie and ham sandwich with grandma. While they were established in 1952, they have really moved with the times, and are now offering a good looking selection of both cabinet and cooked food. The stack was nearing perfection, had the tomatoes been cherry tomatoes instead of giant chunks of grilled tomato, it might have even been perfect. Roast kumara and pumpkin on the side was inspired and delicious, especially with their red pesto. It was a good high stack (check yourself, Jimmy Cooks) and it looked great on the plate. The keto sandwich was made from nice, fresh ingredients, no criticism there, but the cake was a bit of a letdown. The icing was overpoweringly sweet and the cake itself was a little flavourless. Classic cream cheese icing would have been a huge upgrade. The banana smoothie was also flavourless but did have the right texture and temperature. The mocha was clearly made with nice coffee, but was very sweet and - serious points deducted here - had no marshmallows on the side. The whole thing was a slick operation, the interior was clean and modern, the wait staff was very friendly and attentive, and despite being busy the service was fast. Nice one, Robert. Website s

column8: 63/286 Mount Wellington Highway, Mount Wellington, Auckland 1060
column13: UPDATE: Both the Fee-Rex and Business Andy experienced some moderate digestive symptoms within 4 hours of dining at Asia Restaurant. We're not certain that dinner was the cause, so we have not changed their rating, but it still bears mentioning. We ate dinner here in July 2021 Sweet and sour fish with chips and vegetables Roast pork and vegetable curry on rice Glass of milk Asia Restaurant came from the 70's, and they don't make them like this anymore. There are several things that you need to know if you are going to eat at Asia Restaurant. You will not be given water with your meal You will be given two slices of dollar loaf buttered with table spread per person There is no bathroom Everybody eating there except you will be a regular. They will call the hostess by name, and will walk freely in and out of the kitchen Cash only When it's time to pay, you'll need to poke your head into the kitchen to collect the bill. Don't be intimidated by the "Staff" sign on the door, that's just a practical joke for first timers The place is a little run down to say the least, and is honestly a little unwelcoming at first glance. But the food wasn't bad and the service was friendly. The roast pork was pretty tough, the vegetables were boiled, and the curry sauce was okay. But the fish was well fried, and the sweet and sour sauce was reasonable. The dollar loaf was very welcome both for making chip sandwiches and to mop up the curry sauce. Asia Restaurant doesn't have an official website, but there is a fan page

column8: 32 George Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate lunch here in July 2021 Macaroni cheese Nachos Banana smoothie To describe Cafe 40 in 3 S-words: sad, salty and stay away. The place is tired and could use a good clean. The macaroni cheese, while not the worst we've had (congratulations Bees Knees) was overly salty and too rich. The nachos were just another flavourless mince-heap atop the cheapest corn chips money could buy. The "smoothie" was clearly a milkshake that they had blended a banana into and drizzled some honey down the sides of the glass. You're not fooling us, Cafe 40. Cafe 40 does not have a website

column8: CNR ROBERTS & RUAPEHU STREETS, 48 Roberts Street, Taupō 3330
column13: We ate dinner here in July 2021 Cheeseburger with fries Almighty Texan BBQ burger with a hash brown When you look around at a McDonald's, you see a perfect cross section through humanity. Absolutely everybody eats at McDonald's. So well done, Ronald, on becoming a global sensation and appealing to the masses. Not so well done on the food. The meat was a bit dry across the board, the fries were fresh but unsalted, and the hash brown was old and stuck to its paper sleeve. The "almighty" Texan BBQ burger looked a bit sad and had half fallen over in it's box when it arrived via their new-to-us table service. This was probably thanks to the fried onion on the bottom, and although said onion did add a lot to the flavour of the burger, it took just as much away from its structural integrity. The cheeseburger was plain but inoffensive. Website

We ate dinner here in July 2021 Singapore steak with rice Crispy pork massaman curry with rice Thai Orchid boasts the shortest time between ordering and meals arriving of anywhere we've reviewed to date, and that includes McDonalds and Burger King. The service was so fast at first we assumed they had brought the meals to the wrong table. The meals themselves were pretty good. The beef in the Singapore steak wasn't chewy or gristly, but unfortunately there wasn't enough sauce. The massaman was the opposite, plenty of delicious sauce but the meat was dry. Website

column8: 138 The Square, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate lunch here in July 2021 Rice and cauliflower vegetable pie Red pepper, spinach, caramelised onion and feta tart Carrot cake with yoghurt Peanut and banana smoothie Mocha Double Shotz is a better establishment than the Z in its name would imply. Everything was tasty and affordable. There are many ways to make a great banana smoothie. A key factor is that it needs something, it can't just be banana and milk. In this case, they've inventively gone with peanut butter. And it so worked. Had the smoothie been a couple of degrees colder it would have been perfect. The vegetable pie was controversial. Business Andy loved it, while the Fee-Rex was not a fan. We could both agree that it was an inventive and interesting addition to a cafe cabinet, which can frequently be a boring scene. The tart was sweet and delicious, with all components working well together. The cake was moist and tasty, but the icing unfortunately too sweet with not enough cream cheese. The mocha was great. It's a common trap to just pour chocolate into a mocha, but that makes them way too sweet. Double Shotz knows this isn't what you want, and held back on the chocolate resulting in a balanced drink, take notes Robert Harris. Still no marshmallows though. Website

We ate dinner here in July 2021 Pan fried fish, chips, and salad Bangers and mash with peas and onion gravy For the most part, the White Horse Inn stays within its comfort zone. There is a TAB, a handle club, at least four TV's around the bar all playing different channels, and plenty of leaners with Tui towels on them. Their menu is mostly standard pub fare, but they unexpectedly also offer pan fried fish, which we were foolish enough to try. Pan fried fish only works if it is fresh, and this was anything but. We suspect it had come from the freezer. Rubbery, dry, really fishy, it had a nasty skin still on it, and even though it had probably been heated in a pan, it wasn't crispy at all. The chips and salad were fine, but they are irrelevant when the only way that you can stomach the fish is to make each mouthful half tartare sauce. The bangers and mash was a bit better. The bangers themselves were the world's cheapest pork or maybe beef flavoured sausages (who can tell?) from the discount bin, but they were really well cooked. There wasn't enough gravy, although to be honest it wasn't anything to write home about anyway. Website

column8: 189 Papanui Road Shop 13,Inside, Merivale Mall, Merivale, Christchurch 8046
column13: Feta, pine nut and spinach quiche Cheese and onion toastie Apple and caramel muffin Banana smoothie How did you do it, Muffin Break? How did you make the worst banana smoothie we have ever had? Artificial banana syrup, obviously, that's a given. But there was somehow more. Most smoothies made from banana syrup end up tasting like a milkshake. Perhaps Muffin Break make their own signature syrup, from the peels of old bananas and the tears of a Cambodian orphan, creating a blend which is somehow simultaneously too sweet and too bitter. Undrinkable, which was a shame because we both needed some liquid to wash down the other disgusting components of the meal. The cheese and onion toastie never arrived. Instead, a cheese, ham and tomato toastie, which we definitely hadn't ordered, somehow arrived. It was overcheesed, the ham was gross, and had gone soggy on the bottom from sitting too long on the plate. Perhaps this was because it had visited almost every other table before us. Despite the tables being numbered, the wait staff seemed to have no idea which meal went where. We were offered coffees, and then later a cheesy muffin, none of which was ours. The quiche just tasted like old spinach. The feta and pine nuts were visible, but not tasteable. We saw the waitress trying to give our quiche to another table; we wish she had succeeded. The muffin at least was okay. Perhaps Muffin Break had put all of their effort into making their flagship dish passable, leaving no energy for anything else. Pretty tragic. Although not as tragic as how many people were choosing to eat there. The place was packed! We need to band together, stop eating at Muffin Break, and let it die. Website

We ate dinner here in July 2021 Malai kofta with rice Dhaniya adraki paneer with rice Garlic naan Butter naan Aside from the excellent mock kitchen for children set up in the play area, Indian Flavours doesn't do anything to raise its head above the crowd. They did manage to do a few things that dragged them down though. We ordered a plain naan, so were surprised when the world's oiliest butter naan arrived. No exaggeration, there was a literal puddle of butter under the basket when it was taken away. The butter naan had somehow also delaminated into two layers which was bizarre. At least the garlic naan held together, but it too was extremely oily. The curries were inoffensive but bland. The dhaniya adraki paneer had a nice ginger flavour, but not much else going on. The malai kofta was even more plain, apart from the two landmine-like sultanas that provided surprise flavour explosions. The kofta balls were the lowlight; doughy and flavourless. We did at least enjoy the greatest hits of Kishore Kumar wailing in the background. Perhaps the rest of Palmerston North aren't the Kishore fans that we are, as we were the only diners there on a Friday night. Website

column8: 44 The Square, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate dinner here in August 2021 Baked goat cheese, beetroot, rocket, walnuts and crostini Venison with red onion, kale, butternut squash and juniper berry jus Braised short ribs with potato gratin, mushroom cream, charred leek Duck fat potatoes Opera cake with maple and walnut ice cream There are two important historical points you need to know about Dejeuner. In 2020 the head chef at Dejeuner had a heart attack and they have a new head chef In the late 2000s, there used to be a grotty basement bar called Uno at the site where Dejeuner now stands. As is our custom, we arrived at Dejeuner without a reservation. We weren't sure that we would be able to get a table, as we have eaten here under the previous head chef and knew it to be an upmarket, popular spot. The waitress walked us through a refined dining area complete with golden plate awards and quiet music in the background, down the stairs to the basement. What a difference. The first thing you notice is that you are alone. We saw a lot of reserved signs on the tables upstairs, and when we left, upstairs was totally full. Downstairs was dead empty. It was also cold. The wall paper was not wallpaper. Instead it was actual paper featuring an unconvincing brickwork pattern, barely stuck to the wall. There was neon lighting, green around the "brickwork" and multicoloured down the stairs. There was a framed photo of a wine glass decorated with diamantes. There was a $25 fake fire with who-are-you-kidding-flames flickering in it next to a bar heater. The floor was laminate boards that were warped and coming up at the ends which didn't help our already wobbly table. The bar still had the word Uno on the front. There was a television playing a loop of heavily curated Instagram style video from someone's 2017 travel footage. Snorkeling with turtles, waterfalls aplenty, the Eiffel Tower, all accompanied by upbeat beach resort pop music. The music and footage would have been right at home at a Club Med swim-up bar. The side of the basement that contained the bar was curiously empty apart from some stacked chairs. We learned why when were peeking in that area and inhaled, all these years later the smell of Uno's toilets was still lurking in the corner. To top it all off, the wait staff regularly ran up and down the stairs with no apparent regard for how noisy this was. And we mean running - the male server took the steps two at a time. In complete contrast to the decor, the goats cheese entree

column8: 64 George Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Open Adana burger Beef and lamb meze platter Neither Business Andy nor the Fee-Rex had ever tried dolma before, and frankly we won't be trying it again. Be warned, that rolled up seaweed/leaf looking thing on the meze platter might as well be a stick of dynamite. Keep it away from your mouth. That said, the rest of the meze platter was really tasty. Shout out to the homemade falafel. Likewise, the open Adana burger was pretty nice too. We didn't know what Adana was before tonight, turns out it's spicy lamb mince made into a square sausage and cooked on a skewer, and unlike dolma, we'll probably try it again. Whoever was mixing the chili into the mince needs a good talking to though, as the level of heat was quite erratic, from pleasant one mouthful to where's-the-fire-extinguisher the next. As is commonplace with Turkish meals, both meals were generously sized and reasonably priced

We ate lunch here in September 2021 Savoury scone Chicken stack Chocolate cheesecake When we first walked into the Spring Patisserie, we thought it didn't look much like a patisserie. There were far too many pies and sandwiches in the cabinet, and not enough tartes and choux pastry. Are those things in the pie warmer actually delicate cakes that just look like pies and sausage rolls? The food only raised more questions. Why was the savoury scone so sweet? Why was the ham all in one chunk and not mixed throughout? That's not how they make them in Paris. The chicken stack also lacked Parisian flair. For some reason they put a huge thick and solid layer of carrot up top, so when you try to put a fork into it or a knife through it, the innards just smooshed out everywhere. To make matters worse, the chicken was in giant unappetising chunks, and there was far too much mozzarella. In fact any quantity of mozzarella is far too much in a dish such as this, it's a really bland cheese for a start, and when was the last time anyone wanted mozzarella on something that has to be eaten with a knife and fork? A real patisserie wouldn't have made these mistakes. J'Accuse! Spring Patisserie is not a real patisserie at all. You, sir, are a plain Jane kiwi bakery, and not a very good one at that. La cheesecake, trÃ¨s catastrophique. Sorry, forgot you weren't a patisserie. The cheesecake sucked. Website

column8: Inside Woolworths 475 Ti Rakau Drive, Huntington Park, Auckland 2013
column13: We ate lunch here in September 2021 Beef lemongrass bahn mi Beef pho You may remember our review of Saigon Restaurant & Bar where most meals came with chips, save that information for later. Today, the Fee-Rex ordered a rice dish, and they were out of rice. Side note: how does anyone ever run out of rice? It stores forever, it's cheap and readily available, it's not like it takes a long time to cook (and frankly, they had time; there was nobody else there), it was 11:45am and more than one of their meals relied on rice. You're going to have to cook some, so what do you mean, you're out of rice? They offered us chips instead, and it was then that we joined the dots. Saigon Lunch Bar is an offshoot of Saigon Restaurant & Bar, and the apple doesn't fall far from the tree. As was the case in Saigon Restaurant & Bar, the food was so-so. The baguette was way too crisp, the filling was alright, but it was poorly arranged so you couldn't get everything in one bite, much like the tacos at The Gipsy Moth. The pho was reasonable, while it didn't stand out it was enjoyable enough. It would have been nice to have had some water with these meals, for some reason they just left it in the fridge behind the counter. It would have also been nice to have a coffee, but we were informed that the landlord owns the three neighbouring eateries, one of which is Robert Harris. And apparently, only Mr Harris gets to sell coffee. Why they continue to advertise it on the menu is beyond us. It's a chalk board menu, just rub it off man. And then cook some rice. Website

column8: 6/160 Hobsonville Point Road, (Enter from, De Havilland Road, 160 Hobsonville Point Road, Hobsonville, Auckland 0616
column13: We ate dinner here in September 2021 Shahi paneer with rice and plain naan Lamb rajasthani with rice and cheese naan The Fee-Rex has long held a conspiracy theory that multiple dishes on a typical Indian menu are actually the same thing. Indian Summer deepened this conspiracy. Tonight we ordered a shahi paneer, described as "cottage cheese cooked in rich cashew nut gravy and crushed almond." Sounds a bit like a korma, we thought. When it arrived at our table the waitress literally called it a korma. We knew it!! And it was a pale, bland korma at that. Similarly, Business Andy ordered a lamb rajasthani, descibed as "speciality of Rajsthan this unique beef or lamb dish cooked in chefâ€™s special sauce." Chef's special sauce my left nut. Unique my right nut. It was clearly a blend of Maggi tomato soup, some butter chicken, and sugar. We had the same exact dish at Indian2nite where it was called a makhani. The plain naan was pretty good, but the cheese naan was a nightmare. Half of it didn't even have any cheese at all, the other half had way too much, and it was mozzarella to boot. Website

We ate lunch here in September 2021 Steak, cheese, and mushroom pie Eggs benedict with bacon A lot of places like this aren't very good, Sony Cafe doesn't break the mould, they just do what all those similar cafes should be doing. The pie had a nice flaky pastry, it was not soggy at all, and the chunks of steak were tender and not full of gristle although they were perhaps a bit large. The eggs were well poached, and they had drained them before putting the eggs on the nicely toasted muffins. The bacon was well cooked and there was plenty of it, and everything was covered in a generous splash of acceptable hollandaise sauce. Those other cafes like this, where they have the cabinets and the little menu for cooked items are often pretty average. It's pretty easy to just exist and make average food, people will come just because it's an easy and cheap lunch. So it's really nice to see Sony Cafe put in the effort to make good food, and given how busy it was in there, we clearly weren't the only people who had noticed. Sony Cafe has no website.

column8: 61 The Square, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate dinner here in October 2021 Sahi paneer with butter naan and rice Malai kofta with cheese & garlic naan and rice Namaste Bharat was cold, both in temperature and in the disposition of the wait staff. The Fee-Rex ordered a sahi paneer, wondering if it would be different to the shahi paneer she had last week at Indian Summer. The menu described the sahi paneer as 'paneer with sauces and special spices' which didn't offer much of a clue. Turns out sahi paneer is the same as a shahi paneer, in that they are both essentially kormas. It may be that sahi was a typo in the menu. The only noteworthy thing about this otherwise boring curry was that it came with a bizarre sprinkle of grated cheese on top. The malai kofta sauce was very nice. Unfortunately, the koftas themselves were basically two giant balls of mashed potato, and so were pretty stodgy and uninteresting, not like koftas we've had elsewhere. The cheese and garlic naan was pretty good, it did contain some mozzarella but it wasn't the only cheese, and the garlic on top was toasted (a welcome surprise) and well proportioned. The butter naan was a bit thin but was otherwise okay.

We ate lunch here in October 2021 Feta & quinoa pita Greek lamb pizza We are Pita Pit novices.
