While the concept is simple (essentially Subway but with pitas instead of bread), we were ill-prepared and found ourselves panicked in the salad and sauce selection process. The pita wasn't very enjoyable, and it's difficult to know how much of that was our own fault. Were the salads and sauces we selected (fresh capsicum, carrot, beetroot, lettuce, grilled mushroom, cheddar cheese, hummus) a bad blend to accompany the feta & quinoa rosti, or was this pita always destined to be on the flavourless side, regardless of what we did? The Greek lamb pizza, which did not rely on our blundering choices, was great. The flavours worked well together, the lamb was tender, the roast capsicum yummy, and the thin pita base enjoyable. The stringy mozzarella caused some topping loss, which was a shame, but was the only blemish on an otherwise great pizza. Pita Pit offers both dine-in and takeaway, but they're not straining themselves to make dine-in an enjoyable experience. We were given one serviette to share between us, and no plate to catch the inevitable detritus from the meal. Perhaps Pita Pit think that they are creating less work for themselves by providing the bare minimum. This is clearly a false economy, as it causes messy food bits to be dropped all over the table, and with serviettes at a premium we naturally prioritised our own hands and faces over cleaning the table. Website

We ate dinner here in October 2021 Burrrrrito (beef mince burrito with chilli rice and coleslaw) Kiwi joker (ribeye steak with onions, chips, eggs, mushrooms, and coleslaw) Jack Daniel's chocolate fudge pudding Snake bite venom teapot (vodka, Galliano, triple sec, Midori, orange juice, and cranberry juice) Maybe our tastes have changed, but Lone Star isn't like how we remembered it from 2004. Which, incidentally, is about the last time that teapots were cool. That didn't stop us, in a fit of nostalgia, from ordering and then instantly regretting the snake bite venom teapot. Although it was reportedly the waitress's favourite, it was foul. Way too much Galliano, not enough of anything else, and the pulpy orange juice looked chunky and gross in the shot glasses. We stacked the deck a bit here by ordering two items that had been recommended by a friend, and while they were the two strongest dishes, that isn't saying much. The steak was pretty reasonable, well cooked and not gristly, but they put the wrong sauce on it, and the coleslaw was just a slog to get through. The burrito was tragic, it had clearly been premade and then reheated based off the lukewarm temperature, soaked-in tomato sauce, and withered tortilla. The rice was incredibly dry and had not a skerrick of flavour to it, and neither did the endless coleslaw. The other recommendation was a very average chocolate pudding, with rock hard ice cream and not enough sauce. Bookings recommended. Website

column8: 8 George Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: We ate lunch here in October 2021 Fish, chips & coleslaw Brioche French toast with bacon, banana, blueberries, maple syrup and ice cream Banana smoothie At Cafe Jacko we experienced a BAATFR first - finding plastic in our food. This was an unfortunate blip in what was overwise a very nice meal. The fish was delicately battered, the chips well cooked, and the coleslaw tasty (apart from the plastic). The French toast was intense. This isn't your everyday cafe French toast - the brioche was thick, soft and rasisiny, they had battered, fried and sugared the bananas, blueberries were a lovely compote, and who doesn't want ice cream with their breakfast food? Delicious as this was, it was a lot and did become a bit nauseating after a while. The banana smoothie was a standout, and hit the big three of texture, flavour and temperature. Despite the plastic we would happily go back to Cafe Jacko again, and the lovely man at the counter (was it Jacko himself?) was extremely apologetic and comped the affected meal. Website

We ate dinner here in October 2021 Tofu pad thai Beef massaman curry with rice Roti with satay sauce Thai House Express, emphasis on the express. This is among the fastest food that we've been served, right up there with Wendy's. The roti was nice, but what has happened to the satay sauce? It wasn't peanutty at all, more like a watery curry sauce. Speaking of watery curry sauce, the massaman curry wasn't very nice at all. This dish is supposed to be rich and hearty, but it wasn't rich or hearty, and tasted far too strongly of fish sauce and sugar. In contrast, the pad thai was yummy, and we were pleased to see that we were served a tofu pad thai, not a vegetable pad thai featuring tofu. Website

We ate lunch here in October 2021 Beef burger with chips Bruschetta Caramel and chocolate slice Banana smoothie Let's start with the positives. The bruschetta was good, maybe a bit much pesto but it fresh, well put together, and we would happily eat this again. The same cannot be said for anything else that we ordered. The banana smoothie came out promptly and was a good temperature, however it was too milky, it didn't taste much like banana, or really anything else except milk. There was a lengthy wait for the cooked food. Given that we were the only people in the joint, a 25 minute wait just doesn't make any sense. At one point we thought we could smell something burning, so there might have been a do-over. When the food did finally arrive, we could immediately tell that there was something wrong with the burger. The patty was almost cylindrical, the buns were squashed flat and charred, and the whole thing looked like it was ready to fall over. Why do people do this? You want the meat to cover the whole bun, you don't want a small sad dehydrated ball in the middle. The patty's thickness also meant it probably took at least 20 minutes to cook, which will also be why it came out so dry. It was a shame that the patty and buns were so bad as the burger had some nice components like the beetroot relish and caramelised onion. We had saved the slice till last, it looked really good. What a disappointment. The base was about twice as thick as it should have been, and was overpoweringly bitter and dry. The caramel was good, but in these ratios it just couldn't touch the sides. Website

column8: Plaza Shopping Centre, Church Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4412
column13: Palmerston North We ate lunch here in October 2021 Steak and mushroom gourmet pie Cheese and pineapple toasted sandwich Banana cake Options for good dining in the Plaza are limited. So far, the best we've found is Shamiana, and that's not saying much. Phil and Jo's was very popular, in fact many of the cabinet options were all gone by 1 o'clock when we arrived. Unfortunately, this didn't prove to be an indicator that the food was good. The pie was served in a large ramekin, with no pastry and a potato top. We assume this is what made it 'gourmet'. While the flavour of the innards were good, and the mushrooms were distinct, it had been way overcooked causing the potato edges to be rock hard and the bottom of the filling to burn. The steak was really gristly and unpredictable. Phil, Jo, if you're going to buy steak that bad just cut your losses and get mince instead. The toastie was cooked alright, but the amount of crushed pineapple they used was barely detectable. Also, they obviously hadn't wiped the sandwich press as we had a big blurt of relish from another dish cooked onto our sandwich which was unwelcome. The banana cake was pre-cut and plated in the cabinet, and was down to the last piece. It was bone dry on the outside, although the inside which hadn't been exposed to air was okay. It had a thick layer of chocolate icing on the top which contained too much cocoa. Interestingly, it also had a layer of buttercream through the centre. As the outsides were so dry, any extra source of moisture was greatly appreciated. Had the cake not been so dry, this extra buttercream probably wouldn't have brought much to the experience. Website

column8: 2 The Square, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: almerston North We ate dinner here in October 2021 Lamb rack with oxtail cigar, kumara and currant couscous, sweet corn puree Pan fried fish on ginger and kumara cake with Vietnamese slaw Cherry chocolate cheesecake with ice cream Wow, what an incredible fish dish. Everything went together perfectly, it was sweet and tangy, the freshness and varied textures of the slaw were a great accompaniment to the softness of the kumara cake. This is the best fish we've reviewed yet. The lamb rack didn't quite reach the heights of the fish, but was still good. The lamb itself was very nice, and the oxtail cigar was fantastic, but the rest was quite forgettable. The cheesecake was a disappointment. The cherry was undetectable, the texture thick, and the ratio of base to cheesecake mix off kilter. There was a nice vanilla creme with it, but it came with a very confusing strawberry sauce drizzled over the top of it. Website

column8: 7 Atlas Place, Mairangi Bay, North Shore City 0632
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in November 2021 Chicken tender burger with chips Thai beef salad We don't want to say that Business Andy had a privileged upbringing. But this is his first time ever going to a Breakers. You do the maths. Breakers is still a very safe place to bring children, tables of rowdy teens and people with unadventurous tastes. The place had kids running about, was very loud, and the menu was full of safe bets. The burger had some issues. Construction wise it was almost falling over when it came out, requiring a rebuild before eating. The skewer wasn't even through the meat! The crispy chicken coating was so crisp we thought it was either gravel or plastic on first bite. They'd gone overboard with the tomato - 4 slices! The 'aioli' in the burger turned out to just be cheap mayonnaise, and the bun was approaching stale. The salad was better. The meat wasn't gristly, and was only slightly overdone which frankly is better than average for beef strips in a salad. The dressing was tasty and they had lots of crispy noodles which was greatly appreciated. However, some of the lettuce leaves were too big, and there was a layer of ginormous thick cucumber slices, which had been cut diagonally rather than perpendicular They were like frisbees and one came out every time you put your fork in. Website

column8: 3 Campbell Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in November 2021 Newfie poutine Northern spice chicken wings with blue cheese dip Fried cauliflower with ranch and spicy dips Beaver & Bear used to be a fairly successful food truck, so most of what's on the menu is deep fried and delicious. We tried their specialties, and they did not disappoint. The poutine was so hearty, and had stuffing crumbs on top, apparently this is all the rage in Newfoundland. Frankly, it should be like this everywhere. The chicken wings were probably the highlight, they weren't too greasy for a start, and they had a warm spice coating that went very well with the blue cheese dip. The fried cauliflower was very well cooked and came with a hot dipping sauce that was actually delicious, and that's coming from people who don't particularly like spicy sauces. Bookings essential. Website

Palmerston North We ate lunch here in November 2021 Fish, chips and salad Chicken burger with chips Banana smoothie Rumour Has It that this cafe sucks. We can confirm that those rumours are 100% true. Not one element of our meals was enjoyable. The banana smoothie looked appetising when it came out, turns out that was an illusion caused by putting the drink in a pre-chilled glass. The smoothie itself was too warm and full of overpowering banana syrup. The fish was overly fishy fish bites, and the salad soaked in a foul dressing. The chicken burger was a structural nightmare, jenga'd up 5 stories high and impossible to eat as presented. Even after removing some of the chicken and re-skewering it still spilled out everywhere. The chicken was bone dry, the bun generically flavourless. It did contain a hash brown, which we feel is an under-utilised burger element, but that didn't come close to saving it. Even the chips were offensive. They had about 10% the flavour of a normal chip and tasted like stale nothing. Yes they were unsalted, which didn't help, but it was more than that. How exactly they achieved this feat we'll never know, as we sure as hell won't be going back to find out. Website

column8: 161 The Square, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in November 2021 Vegetable okonomiyaki Teriyaki beef donburi Although the decor was dated and the food service was slow, Hanamizuki serves good food. The okonomiyaki was nommy with a good combination of sauces. The donburi vegetables were fresh, the meat tender. The sesame on the spinach was a standout. Website

Feilding We ate lunch here in November 2021 Big breakfast Breakfast muffin Banana smoothie The staff at Delish Cafe are delightful, they complimented Business Andy's shorts, and apologised for the wait even though we hadn't been waiting very long. The breakfast muffin was great, it was like an elevated version of a McMuffin. A juicy beef patty with melted cheese, tomato sauce, hash brown, and a fried egg in a toasted English muffin. It was magnificent, and very reasonably priced. The big breakfast was truly big, and was well executed. The hash browns deserve a special shout out, and perhaps the tomato could have been roasted a little longer, but the rest of the components were all really good. The banana smoothie was a real let down, they had doused the sides of the glass with banana syrup which ruined it. Website

column8: 17 Victoria Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate lunch here in December 2021 Braised lamb neck crepe Pork dumplings Banana, peanut butter, and cacao smoothie Despite a rocky start, our meal at Amayjen was fantastic. On arrival we were tersely instructed to present our vaccine passes "before we touched anything" like we were children with chocolate on our hands. They also took ages to take our order, then lied to us about the reason. The first server told us they were looking for their mask, and the second server told us that they were a member of staff down. Neither of these is particularly believable, as we had just watched them both have a long conversation together after taking someone else's order. Fortunately for everyone, the food was absolutely fantastic. The lamb crepe was meaty, hearty, and full of flavour. And the pork dumplings were excellent as well. The smoothie scored full marks for both texture and temperature, a rarity. Website

column8: 38/60 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in December 2021 Beef and lamb iskender Falafel doner It was an extremely quiet night at Fire Home, maybe they had taken the opportunity to leave a skeleton crew. The one member of staff appeared quite inexperienced, she didn't know where the buttons were on the till and couldn't keep up with a normal pace of ordering. She also seemed not to know what comes with an iskender. The menu advertised meat, rice, salad, hummus, jacik, and sauce, however the plate contained only meat, rice, and sauce, and looked a little underwhelming. The meat was very dry, and we noted that their rotisserie meat stands were empty, so we assume this has come from the fridge. Five to ten minutes later, when Business Andy's kebeb showed up, we found out that this poor staff member also didn't know how to wrap a doner. They really shouldn't have been left there alone. The foil was all scrunched up on one side, it was completely wrapped instead of open at one end, wasn't in a bag, and wasn't on a plate. The net result was that you had to tear open a foil package that didn't tear open well and was also too hot to handle. Opening the foil was like tearing a hangnail off your finger, you pull a little and nothing happens, so you pull more and then a whole chunk of scrunched side foil comes off bringing with it a long and painful tail that just ruins your day. There was sauce all over Business Andy's hands, and a hell of a mess left on a food court tray. To their credit, the flavour was alright. And at least it had salad. Fire Home has no website.

column8: 415 Ferguson Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in December 2021 Onion rings Memphis BBQ Big Angus burger Original Big Angus (single patty) Carl's Jr is what Burger King was meant to be. The burgers were reasonable, the onion rings were actually real onion in a batter (shame about having too much salt). The Memphis BBQ was better than the Original Big Angus, with the crispy onion bits being a highlight. However, the patties were on the dry side, the sauce distribution and flavour in the Original Big Angus were poor. However, good construction and good buns were also at play. We appreciated the paper wrapped around the burger, but where the heck were the serviettes! Overall this was the best traditional fast food chain we've been to yet, although still not good enough to crack a 3. Website

column8: 74 Rawhiti Road, One Tree Hill, Auckland 1061
column13: Taihape We ate lunch here in December 2021 Beef sausage roll Potato top pie Churros The decor at Coffee Plus + makes it look like a cross between a bar, a second hand furniture shop, and someone's rumpus room. There is also a very sweet and very obese dog called Brie whom we liked very much. They didn't make any of their food, they just heated it up for us. But that said, they had taken some care. This was no casual microwave job, both the sausage roll and the pie were crisp indicating that they had been in some kind of oven. The churros were completely covered in cinnamon sugar, chocolate sauce, and caramel sauce, and while they were good, I mean come on, they were always going to be good, we've had better. The churros were the only thing that didn't reheat well, unlike the pie and sausage roll, they really needed to be deep fried fresh. Website

Ohingaiti Crumbed chicken burger Curly fries Mince & cheese pie Flat Hills Cafe caters to the passing through crowd - cars travelling north from Palmy who are too hungry or lazy to wait for Taihape, families who need somewhere to stop for the kids to burn off some energy, and Intercity buses. Credit where credit is due, Flat Hills knows what it is and has provided. Heaps of parking for buses, motorhomes etc. A sizeable selection of cooked, cabinet, and readymade food (ice creams, chocolate bars etc). Accessible, plentiful and clean bathrooms. Fun stuff for children - animals to look at, a bouncy castle, swings, even a maze. Unfortunately, the food just isn't that good. The highlight was the curly fries - oh my God there were so many big curlies. We've all been disappointed before when you buy a bowl of 'curly fries' that is actually a bowl of sad half moons with maybe one 520 degree curly. Not this bowl, it was mostly real curlies, an absolute delight. But it was downhill from there. The accompanying aioli was flavourless and had a little skin on the top like it had been pre-poured. The pie had good pastry on top, but not so good for the base and a distinct I've-been-in-this-warmer-for-some-time flavour and texture. The burger was sad. Not only did it not contain any onion rings as advertised, it was poorly constructed, had unwelcome surprise tomato and just didn't taste very good. Website

Palmerston North We ate lunch here in January 2022 Campfire smash Cauliflower tacos Banana smoothie Passionfruit smoothie Cafe Cuba has been one of the most popular cafes in Palmerston North for the past 20 years. They have a diverse menu, speedy service and a reputation for being reliably good. In the Fee-Rex's expert opinion, it was home to the best smoothie in Palmerston North. We say was as unfortunately the smoothie game has slipped a bit. Don't get us wrong, they're still good, but they are no longer great. The passionfruit smoothie used to be tangy and creamy, really cool and thick with honey down the sides. Today's passionfruit smoothie was almost too tangy, much less creamy with more of a juice consistency. The banana smoothie was perfectly acceptable, but lacked in va va voom. The campfire smash, which is egg, potato, onion, spinach all cooked up together with a piece of ciabatta, was again good but not great. The tacos were disappointing, plain and thoughtless. They seemed like the kind of tacos you would make and home, eat then go "well, at least I'm not hungry anymore but I won't make that again." Step up Cafe Cuba! You've earned a 3 rating today but we know you can do better. Bookings recommended Website

column8: 81 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 5301
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in December 2021 Curry puffs Tofu pad thai Lamb massaman curry with rice Caramel bubble tea What a weird pad thai. Admittedly it was a vegan pad thai, so we were prepared for it to be a little different (no egg, maybe a little different flavour from no fish sauce). But veganism doesn't preclude the pad thai staples of peanuts and lemon, both of which were absent. And you certainly don't make up for a lack of animal products by drowning the dish in oil, which this was. Very disappointing. The curry was better, with a nice sauce and meat that was tender, pretty reasonable on the lamb-you-find-in-a-cheap-curry scale. Peanuts were again a problem. There were upleasant peanut sinkers all at the bottom of the meal which had been "toasted" by someone who didn't appreciate toasted peanuts. They had been grilled at way too high a temperature for a very short time, which had served just to put a bit of colour on the outside of what were in essence raw peanuts. For some reason the caramel bubble tea tasted like coffee as much as caramel. At least the curry puffs were good, nice pastry and flavour. Website

column8: 218 Broadway Avenue, City Centre, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North Lamb's fry with bacon Steak salad with feta balls Banana smoothie Cafe Brie was a real mix of the good, the bad, and the ugly. The good: The smoothie was one of the best that we have reviewed. Understated, cold, perfectly smooth, and utterly delicious. The feta balls were fantastic and unexpected, a real treat. The brown onion and mushroom jus that came with the lamb's fry was dark, hearty, and very tasty. The bad: The steak was overcooked, we asked for medium but received well done steak. The liver was unevenly cooked, most was a bit overdone, and a part of it was quite underdone. The ugly: The kumara. It was a bit overdone when it was roasted, and from the texture of it, that was at least three days ago. They were hard as rocks, and very unpleasant. And this was a real shame because the kumara is often the bit of a salad that you really look forward to. Website

Palmerston North We ate dinner here in January 2022 Pulled pork tacos Beef enchiladas Churros with caramel sauce and ice cream Libre is Palmerston North's premiere Mexican eatery, with a nice casual vibe and great cocktails. The food was good to excellent, with the tacos being the highlight. Have your serviette at the ready, you will get sauced. The churros were delicious too, but they were just churros and could have been a little more fluffy and a little more inventive. Bookings recommended

column8: 159 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in January 2022 Bruschetta Beef tartar Fries with truffle and parmesan Seasonal greens - cabbage Korean fried chicken "Lemon pie" with sorbet This place is really made for sharing, they offer small plates, which is all we ordered, and large plates which serve two to three people. Even the desserts are made to be shared, so it's tapas really, even if they don't say that they are. Speaking of sharing, if you are hoping to share a conversation, be aware that the acoustics in Provenance are pretty bad. The general noise level was so loud that we struggled to hear each other at times. The food was excellent, it is on the fancy side but not overpriced, apart from the dessert which was a total rip-off. The bruschetta was a little different, it came with roast garlic and whole roast tomatoes for a "some assembly required" dish. The beef tartar was very flavoursome, and was accompanied by a host of unusual but welcome bedmates. The fries really stood out, they had gone crazy with the parmesan and truffle oil, and the truffle butter on the side was just divine. Honestly it was a struggle not to mop up the remainder with our fingers. The chicken had a sweet chilli vibe, and didn't have a thick crispy coating like a lot of fried chicken does. So it was a bit different to what we expected, but was delicious nonetheless. The lemon pie was their only misstep. It was completely deconstructed, and had way more sorbet than anything else. While the ingredients were all excellent, we would have preferred half the sorbet, and double the amount of the other components. Bookings recommended. Website

BusinessAndy&FeeRex Cravings Cafe 187 Palmerston North We ate lunch here in January 2022 Crispy chicken burger with curly fries Kumara rosti with haloumi and egg Banana smoothie If you are pregnant, then this is the cafe for you, situated right in the birthing complex, and full of pregnant women. Maybe not full to the brim, but there was definitely an overrepresentation of gravid uteri the day that we were there. The food at Cravings Cafe was actually pretty good, and there were plenty of other things available that we would have liked to try. The chicken was very crispy, perhaps a little dry, but the burger overall was excellent. Very well constructed, and the curly fries, which come standard with the burger were top notch. The menu didn't even say that the fries were curly, but damn were they curly, with several very large curlies present. The rosti was made with orange kumara rather than the usual purple which was a nice change. The haloumi was well cooked but very thin, too thin to squeak, as it turned out. The banana smoothie wasn't good at all, unfortunately. It wasn't a banana smoothie at all, it was some kind of mix of tropical fruits and was just very sweet. The great texture and temperature were hard to appreciate with that flavour. Website

Palmerston North We ate dinner here in January 2022 Buffet Chinatown Chinese Restaurant offers both a buffet and an a la carte menu. As we walked in the dude said "buffet?" We didn't know better so we went with it, but when we looked out into the restaurant, we saw a bit of a trend appear. There was a few tables where people had ordered off the menu, and all but one was Asian diners. We suspect that they knew something that we didn't. The buffet wasn't all bad, the stand outs were the vegetarian noodles, the fish bites, and the chicken wings. Standing out for the wrong reasons were the pan fried dumplings, the BBQ pork, and the pork curry. The rest of the things that we tried were middling to bad, the prime example of this category was the under seasoned onion rings. There was dessert on offer, which was nice, the carrot cake was the best part, the cheesecake, the worst by a considerable margin. Website

Palmerston North We ate lunch here in January 2022 Smashed avo on toast with a poached egg Baked potato with mince We'll talk about these meals in the order that they arrived. The smashed avo on toast was middling, the toast itself was thick, soft, and fresh. It came with a very welcome slice of lemon, which paired well with the avocado itself. Unfortunately, the poached egg was underdone and a bit sloppy. And extra unfortunately, there was a huge piece of lettuce under the avo, on the toast. We really don't know who wants this, it was entirely unnecessary. This space represents the gap between us finishing the avo on toast, and the arrival of the baked potato. The potato itself was not underdone, but lacked fluffiness. We carefully avoided the vegetarian mince option because it contained red beans and chickpeas, so we were quite upset when the beef mince arrived with both red beans and chickpeas. Admittedly these both didn't taste like much, but that's not a compliment. Could have used a little more sour cream, extra points for the sweet chilli sauce on the top. Website

column8: MGMR+7G5, Patul Rd, City of Santiago, 3311 Isabela, Philippines
column13: Palmerston North We ate lunch here in February 2022 Big breakfast Jackfruit burger We haven't been somewhere this shambolic since The Cooperage Cafe, and Cafe Royale was even worse. When we arrived we were fourth in the queue. Ten minutes later we were still fourth in the queue. It was immediately obvious that the cafe was disastrously understaffed, with just two servers running around with their heads on fire instead of taking the orders of the people who were waiting. As can happen when the world is ending, these two were just doing the next thing that appeared in front of them like putting chairs nicely around tables, and stacking the menus in their holder. Priorities, ladies! There was a bizarre queuing system at play. You had to bags a table by leaving your coat or umbrella on it before then queuing up for all eternity. We suppose that they wanted to avoid people getting in the queue, waiting, and then finding out that there were no tables, but frankly they were causing that problem themselves with their glacial service. We had been standing around in the queue for quite a long time when it finally started to move. We were given menus and only one minute later expected to order when we found ourselves at the fabled front of the queue facing a harassed looking server. Perhaps they cater exclusively to speed readers, because the menu was the most packed in and poorly laid out four pages that we've ever seen. Neither of us had read even half the menu, and we panic picked the first thing that sounded alright. We could see the flames around the server's head begin to burn hotter and brighter as she struggled to find what Business Andy had ordered in the POS system. We had to point it out on the physical menu, at which time we found out that it wasn't actually available, not just that day, but ever. Cross it out you numptys! Business Andy was scanning for something new to order when he was accosted by the question, "are you vegan?" After answering no, the menu was literally snatched out of his hands by the server, who was completely engulfed in flames at this point, and cried shrilly "that's the vegan menu!" While we appreciated that she was attempting to simplify what was a very stressful process, non-vegans are actually allowed to order vegan food. In fact we had just ordered two vegan meals right in front of her. The flames were licking at us, and we panic ordered a big breakfast without reading through what was in it. The wait
column16: nothingness, but its juice had spread across the
column18: other food item. This was a real shame

column8: 111 Devon Street East, New Plymouth Central, New Plymouth 4310
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in February 2022 Dirty Duke BBQ Cheeseburg Onion rings Fried cauliflower Giving ReBurger a rating was quite difficult for us. There is something inherently enjoyable about a burger and fried stuff, which sometimes inclines the Fee-Rex to give a place a higher rating than it perhaps deserves. However, the fact of the matter is that we'd both like to go back and eat another ReBurger, so that means that they fall into the 3 (good) category. Their fellow 3's, Burgerfuel and Shake Out are superior, but ReBurger doesn't belong in the same tier as McDonald's and Carl's Jr. Both burgers were cut from the same, BBQ-ey cloth, the Dirty Duke had a thicker patty, some bacon, and some pickles, but they were otherwise quite similar. They were well constructed, with fresh buns, and well cooked meat patties. The aioli was much more noticeable in the BBQ Cheeseburg, and was sorely missed in the Dirty Duke. The onion rings were hearty, real onion, and a good size, however they were desperately missing a dipping sauce. There was tomato sauce freely available, but that's just not the right accompaniment for an onion ring. Perhaps if we had been given some aioli, we wouldn't have noticed the oily taste in the batter so much. We really liked that they did fried cauliflower, and they were well sized pieces of actual cauliflower instead of just balls of cauliflower mush. They had been criminally over salted, but were really nice otherwise. Website

column8: 94 Broadway Avenue, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in April 2022 Banana smoothie Iced vanilla Diablo pizza Beef & lamb iskender It's so strange that there are two Turkish/Italian places to eat at in Palmerston North. Similar to Viva Cafe & Bar, Cafe Eminem is trying to be equal parts Turkish restaurant and Italian restaurant, and excelling at neither. Their decor was trying-to-be-fancy-while-not-spending-any-money chic, prominently featuring a fountain right in the middle of the restaurant that was not connected to any water. Cafe Eminem was quiet when we got there, calm and ready to drop bombs, which they did in the form of two very disappointing beverages. The banana smoothie was clearly just crushed ice and ancient bananas, it was the colour of banana cake mix and about as thick. While we applaud the use of paper straws, and appreciate they at least gave wide bore straws, such straws just couldn't handle the fortitude of these drinks. About half way through the drink the straws were completely collapsed. We tried tearing the straw, and turning it upside down, to no avail. The iced vanilla tasted like a watered down McDonald's milkshake and was just as thick as the smoothie. The iskender wasn't too bad. Could have used more salad, and points off for not having any Turkish bread, but at least there was plenty of sauce, the rice was fresh and the meat wasn't dry. The pizza was very heavy on the mozzarella, to the point of stringy absurdity at times. It was pretty flavourless, with the salami being beyond mild, and the onion was raw. Website

Palmerston North We ate lunch here in April 2022 Banana smoothie Beef stroganoff with rice Beef burger and chips The Verdict has been around since 1989 and has recently moved to a cursed building opposite Palmerston North City Council. Will they be able to survive atop the corpses of so many unfortunate cafe's? While we weren't impressed by The Verdict, there were plenty of people there who apparently were. The banana smoothie committed two very serious offences. One was containing banana syrup. The other, even more heinous, was being insufficiently blended with large chunks of banana sitting at the bottom rendering the last inch undrinkable. It's a shame because they had done some things right - the smoothie was large, and a great temperature and texture. But these two sins cannot be forgiven. The stroganoff came from a bain-marie which had a fly hovering around it. Just in case it isn't clear, flies on food = points off. It wasn't really bad, but wasn't good either. And where's the sour cream? The burger was tragically over-saladed. Three huge pieces of tomato. Four giant thick cut diagonal pieces of cucumber. And a full one inch tutu of lettuce protruding around the burger. While the salad was fresh, it was just way, way too much. It completely overshadowed the good elements of the burger, such as melty cheese, a fresh brioche bun, a moist tasty patty and some reasonable sauce. The chips had the flavour and texture of fairground cup-of-chips. It's hard to describe exactly what was different about them, maybe the oil was old? Regardless, they weren't great. The verdict on The Verdict? Meh. Website

Palmerston North We ate dinner here in April 2022 Bruschetta Panfried fish on Greek salad with potatoes Coconut bubble tea with blueberry bubbles What is Flavour? A restaurant that kind of thinks it's fancy? A karaoke bar? A brunch spot? An ice cream parlour? A takeaway coffee joint? Yes, yes, yes, yes, and yes. As is almost always the case, when somewhere tries to be all things to all people, it ends up being not much. That said, the bruschetta was pretty good. It had giant pieces of tomato on it, which is normally a bad sign, but they pulled it off. The bread was thick, fresh and warm, the ratio of pesto, balsamic and feta was about right. The bubble tea was also pretty good, especially the exploding blueberry bubbles. The fish was not great. The problem wasn't necessarily the fish itself, but the sides. Where were the potatoes? There were literally two pieces of potato in that bowl. And the salad had way too many big whole olives. Maybe if we were reviewing karaoke bars, or ice cream parlours, Flavour would have fared better. But as a dinner spot, while not a disaster, we wouldn't go back again. Website

column8: 68 The Square, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in April 2022 Tofu and shitake mushrooms with rice Pork belly with rice Honey and lemon tea If you manage to impress The Fee-Rex with a plate of vegetables, you're doing something right. While the carrot was overcooked, and the onion undercooked, the sauce was dynamite. The tofu and the rice were both good too. The pork belly was a bit dry, and while it came with a little bit of a salad, the dish was a bit bare-bones overall. It did come with good rice, and another explosive sauce though. The honey and lemon tea had a bit of marmalade at the bottom, and came in the world's cutest cup with a little lid and an adorable teaspoon, we thoroughly enjoyed putting his wee hat back on him after each sip. Website

Palmerston North We ate lunch here in April 2022 Banana smoothie Potato rosti with salad Fried chicken with shoestring fries and salad Melting moment Being part of the unpopular food court is tough, but Nourish Cafe & Deli isn't doing much to elevate their station. The banana smoothie was a good temperature, but it was bland and far too thin. The rosti was exciting at first, it was nice to see something different in a cabinet, but it quickly became tiresome as the texture was quite claggy. The only flavour came from the sour cream and sweet chilli sauce that had been generously applied, and the side salad was fresh but boring. The exact same salad featured on the side of the fried chicken, which was fine, but the team at Nourish had clearly forgotten the secret herbs and spices. Shoestring fries were a nice change from the current thick cut paradigm, and there was plenty of mayo for dipping. The highlight was the melting moment. It was fresh and crumbly, and was neither too sweet nor not sweet enough. The icing had a nice soft texture and there was just the right amount of it. We would happily eat this cookie again, which can't be said for the rest of our meal. Website

Feilding We ate lunch here in May 2022 Fish tacos with salad Fried mushrooms on toast Passionfruit and orange smoothie We were surprised to see a clientele of 80%+ grey tops when we walked in, but don't let that paint a picture of one of those old lady cafes with the pie warmers and red plastic trays. The cabinet was actually quite interesting, although we elected to order off the menu. The fish tacos were the weaker offering, the fish itself was just frozen hoki sticks, and while they had toasted the tacos and the chipotle mayo was pretty good, this dish was dragged down by its salad. The side salad was completely undressed, not even a dash of the most basic vinagrette. That's bad enough until you realise that the salad was an add-on to the tacos and cost an additional $3.50. How very dare you!? An undressed salad is a crime, and being charged for it as a separate item is cause for the reintroduction of capital punishment. Seriously, fuck you, $3.50 for that? Not two blocks over, Empire Sports and Garden Bar Restaurant blows this place out of the water on value for money. The mushrooms on toast were actually pretty good. We opted for fried over creamy and were not disappointed. The mushrooms were nicely garlicky, and came with two good thick slices of toast that had been slightly overdone but were still delicious. Extra points that the little butter packets were soft enough to spread, not the usual rock hard straight from the fridge ordeal. The smoothie really should have been a juice. The flavours were weird, and the addition of orange juice meant that it kept separating into a foam layer and a juice layer. Not cool. Website

Wellington Venison meatballs Cheese fondue with bread Chips Leuven is very Belgian, and they are taking their beer game seriously. This isn't just some bar that's serving Stella and calling it a day, there were literally dozens of different beers. The meatballs were juicy and not too pungent or gamey, with a good tomato sauce. The fondue was very tasty, but absurdly stingy with the bread. It was annoying and confusing to run out of dipping materials one fifth of the way through the fondue. Thankfully we had a bowl of chips, which were thick cut and well suited to dipping. But you shouldn't have to order an extra side to compensate for insufficient bread! And even with the chips Business Andy still ended up bringing down the tone of the establishment by finishing it off with a spoon. Website

Feilding We ate dinner here in June 2022 Khao phad with tofu Gaeng Panaeng with beef and rice You may have noticed a pattern when Business Andy and The Fee-Rex visit Thai places. The Fee-Rex almost always orders a tofu pad thai, and Business Andy generally orders a Massaman Curry. Tonight we decided to branch out, and we were not rewarded. The khao phad, which is fried rice with scant vegetables, was passable. The rice itself tasted a bit oily, but the tofu was top notch and it came with lime which was very welcome. The gaeng panaeng, which is supposed to be a rich peanut flavoured curry, was disgusting. To be more specific, the meat was revolting. Chewy, rubbery, gristly, fatty, bleugh. The sauce was bland. And the waitress waited until the curry was on the table before asking us if we wanted to order rice. At least the food came out quick, but that just meant we found out how expensive it was faster. Fifty dollars for a mediocre fried rice and a gross curry, not cool. Website

column8: 55A Joseph Street, West End, Palmerston North 4412
column13: Palmerston North Feta and blue cheese tart Calzone with meat New York cheesecake Banoffee (banana and coffee) smoothie The Joseph Street Kitchen, or JSK as the locals say, was a bit frantic. It was being staffed by two stressed out older ladies who informed us they were very short staffed and that only the cabinet menu and eggs were available. Luckily the cabinet was brimming with good-looking choices. The tart was sensational, light and fluffy, great flavour with enough blue cheese in it to make it blue-cheesy, but still had a nice sharp flavour like the feta too. It was paired with a little grated beetroot salad which went really well with the tart, and a relish too. The 'calzone with meat' was poorly named but tasted good. The construction was interesting. JSK offers both a vegetarian and a meat calzone. They're the same product, with both being stuffed with mushroom and having cheese on top, but the meat one had bacon on top too. Was it really a calzone? It certainly wasn't pretty, but it definitely got the job done. The highlight was the New York cheesecake which was a hands down 10/10. The base was a great texture and just the right thickness. The body had a great flavour and texture, silky and delicious. Paired nicely with the side yoghurt too. The banoffee smoothie was a let down. It was more like an average iced coffee. You could barely detect the banana, and the texture was very thin. Website

column8: shop 5/687 Fergusson Drive, Elderslea, Upper Hutt 5018
column13: Upper Hutt Reshmi paneer with rice and plain naan Malai kofta with rice and cheese naan Yatra was a funny mix of highs and lows. The instantly noticeable low on arrival was the ambiance, or lack thereof. 7.45 on a Friday night and we were the only people dining in, with individuals passing in and out sometimes for takeaways. Practically as silent as a grave. And whereâ€™s the Bollywood jams? It was so quiet that it was uncomfortable, and made you feel like you couldnâ€™t talk. It also made the noise of the hardest working chef in the kitchen very clear. Chef Mic(rowave). He was constantly beeping away, door opening and closing. This seemed very unusual. Weâ€™ve watched enough Kitchen Nightmares to know Chef Mic doesnâ€™t belong in a commercial kitchen, and this restaurant had two, front and centre right by the pass. And they were working simultaneously. What was going in there? We did see our rice pop out of Chef Mic - why was the rice being reheated? How old was it? The Fee-Rex used to work at an Indian Restaurant that re-heated its rice, and that place was absolutely disgusting. The other big fail was the malai kofta. The sauce was totally flavourless, and the koftas were unusual. They were big turds of stodgy potato with sultanas in the centre. The plain naan was peculiar too, it was somehow extra plain and pretty dry. Was it made with wholewheat flour? We are pleased to report, however, that Yatra had the best cheese naan Business Andy has had in years. No mozzarella! Actual cheese with flavour! It wasnâ€™t quite perfect, it could have used more cheese and better distributed too. But in a field of stringy flavourless naan, this one definitely stood above the rest. The reshmi paneer sauce was good too, earthy and rich. It was let down by the presence of wilted old capsicum (to give you an indicator of texture, on initial chewing we thought it was mushroom - perhaps Chef Mic had prepared it), and they had fried the paneer which was controversial. Website

Sanson Boysenberry cream horn Pork riblet roll Chips Viv's Kitchen is a Sanson institution, with its iconic giant cream horn on proud display on State Highway 1. Unsurprisingly, the place was packed. Unfortunately, the experience failed to live up to the hype. The chips were particularly disappointing, they were dry and floury. Dousing them in sauce to remedy this backfired, as the sauce was the cheapest watery tomato sauce available; our friend's description of the sauce as being "straight from 1993" was apt. The pork riblet roll was a little controversial, as The Fee-Rex thinks pork riblet is disgusting at the best of times. Business Andy, being the most basic of bitches thought it was pretty good though. As to the signature dish, the cream horn, it was fresh and choccablock with real cream as it should be. But did it send us singing from the hilltops, no. Website

Waiouru We ate lunch here in October 2022 Beef nachos Cinnamon, marscapone and blueberry bagel Banana smoothie The Mess Tent is the cafe at the Waiouru Army Museum, the kind of place you stop for lunch when you're driving down State Highway 1. It's clean and tidy, bathrooms, a big carpark and a tank that kids can play on, which is all that a lot of travelling families require. But we have more discerning tastes, and we won't stand for anywhere skating by on convenience alone. The smoothie was truly criminal. Chunks of ice. Too thin. Sour taste from the yoghurt. No good banana flavour, probably a green banana. Very unpleasant. The nachos were better, good chips, reasonable mince, but there weren't enough chips for the amount of mince present. They'd made some special effort on the bagel, which was much appreciated, especially as this can be a real throwaway menu item. But they'd perfectly buttered it, added some cinnamon, and the marscapone and blueberries were spot on. Unfortunately our souls had already been crushed by the smoothie, which made it hard to enjoy anything. You'd be better off going to The Rustic Eating House. Website

Thorndon, Wellington We ate dinner here in December 2022 Pastrami bagel Pork sausage, fennel seed, mushroom, and red onion pizza You know a restaurant has a sad vibe when you walk in and ask if the kitchen is open. What a dive. Looks like this place was built 20 years ago and hasn't been cleaned or had any maintenance since. The food was okay, although they might have been a bit heavy handed with the fennel seeds on the pizza. Bit of a buzz-kill overall. Website

column8: Wellington Railway Station, Cnr Featherston Street & Platform, 1 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011
column13: Pipitea, Wellington Seasoned wedges with salsa and sour cream Nacho chips with beef mince, cheese, salsa, and sour cream Trax is located in the busy Wellington train station and caters to the commuter crowd. As such, their prime meal times are breakfast and lunch. In the evenings they focus on drinks for folks at the end of the day before their trip home. Figuring they will have a meal waiting for them, they only serve bar snacks in the evening. And fair enough. But Trax, there's no reason those bar snacks can't be good. We watched with horror as our wedges sat on the pass (not even under a heat lamp) for an inordinate amount of time while the chips were being cooked. It's fry cook 101, you need to time your frying so dishes are done at about the same time. Unsurprisingly the wedges were tepid. They had also been slathered in a very boring salsa, we would much rather have had the option to dip. The sour cream was on the side, where it belonged, and was a good amount and texture. The nacho chips were a bummer. There was very little mince, and what was there wasn't pleasant. Who puts cooked carrot cubes in nacho mince? There also wasn't a lot of cheese, and the same unfortunate salsa was present. At least they'd got the sour cream right a second time in a row. Trax, you should put in some effort, or stop doing bar snacks. You should also clean your carpet, it stinks in there. Website

Pipitea, Wellington Grilled lemongrass beef with rice and salad Yellow curry with beef and rice Iced coffee with condensed milk Perhaps the best thing that the French have ever done was introduce coffee to Vietnam. We loved the iced coffee, it was deliciously coffee-ey, which was balanced out nicely by the condensed milk. We expected a bit more beef to be in the curry, which was good otherwise. It was a very delicate and interesting flavour, and the vegetables were fine, but where was the beef? We only found about three or four small pieces in there. To be fair, the meat is often the worst part of a curry, so it's not like we were really upset, it just wasn't quite what we expected. Perhaps they blew their beef budget on the lemongrass beef dish, which was essentially a large pile of slightly sus beef, with salad and rice on the side. The beef was dry fried, was perhaps a bit overdone, and was definitely a bit gristly. The salad's dressing was in a separate bowl, a nice touch. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate breakfast here in December 2022 Mushroom pizza bread Vanilla, peach tea, and strawberry donut Chai latte Banana, peanut butter, and cacao smoothie Lunch money did some things quite well. The service was fast and super friendly. There is no cooked menu, but their cabinet had quite a few items in it that looked nice. The donut was pretty good, although half the glaze fell off it as we ate. The drinks were middling, and unfortunately the pizza bread was burnt. You can't serve something that blackened and hope to get anything higher than a 2. Website

Arancini balls Pork belly Fried cauliflower Duck liver pate Chocolatete mousse dome Creme brûlée At Latitude 37 everything was good, but nothing was excellent. Across the board there were no standouts in either direction, it was just universally enjoyable. They could do with turning the music down a few decibels as you definitely had to shout especially once the live music started. And shout to their cocktail menu, especially the clockwork orange.

column8: 210A left bank, Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011
column13: We ate dinner here in January 2023 Vegan shared meal for three Mother of Coffee is an Ethiopian restaurant, and a new cuisine for Business Andy and the Fee-Rex. The shared meal was 4 lentil and chickpea dishes, one dish of extremely hot chilli, and a flat grey fluffyish pancake each, which you tear and dip into the curries. There was plenty of food - we bought extra pancakes which was a mistake. The flavours were good and diverse, and the pancake was a fun dining experience. It would have been nice if the pancake was made fresh, it was a bit on the cool side. Website

Tawa, Wellington We ate dinner here in February 2023 Orange beef & rice Mee goreng Yum Yum House is your typical westernised Chinese joint. They have dispensed with the chicken feet and jellyfish, but have kept all your fried favourites. The decor was, to put it generously, dated. We're talking floral embroidered chairs with shiny thread, plastic grapes and valences hanging from the ceiling. It was none too clean either, with the Fee-Rex finding a used serviette on her seat and plenty of rice under the table. Perhaps as a result of this, dine-in was empty and the restaurant was quiet except for the owners child being entertained by the young teenage wait staff. While the mood in the restaurant wasn't cheerful, the meals sure were cheap. The orange beef sauce was overly sweet. However, they had done a number of things right. The meat wasn't gristly, it was well fried, they'd added sesame seeds, the onion and carrot were cut small, and the lettuce was fresh. The three (!) meats that came with the mee goreng weren't quite the same calibre, but were passable, and didn't ruin what was otherwise a reasonable dish. Website

Tawa, Wellington Malai kofta with rice and plain naan Bombay aloo with rice and cheese & garlic naan The decor in this place was ðŸ”¥. Literally. As in, the place had been on fire. There were smoke stains up the walls and soot all over the ceiling. Perhaps this was why they left the door open sweeping in icy night air for the entire meal. They didn't really seem to give any consideration to the idea that people might like to dine in. To be fair, take away is clearly their bread and butter and they were doing a very steady trade. Strangely, they didn't ask us how hot we wanted our curries. Instead they just bought us whatever, which was one mild and one medium. The malai kofta (mild) was insanely sweet. Even the koftas themselves were sweet, but had a heck of a texture, so bouncy and soft. Those sweet koftas in a less sugary sauce could have been a great dish. The Bombay aloo came out medium. It also came out boiled, despite the menu explicitly stating the potatoes would be deep fried. It was otherwise okay. The naans were pretty good. They were both soft and bready, not too much cheese with the garlic, and a nice sprinkling of herbs and some oil on the plain. Watch out when it's time to pay though - we were accidentally (or intentionally?) overcharged by like 40%. Worse still, we didn't realise until we were half way home and too lazy to turn around. Website

Thorndon, Wellington Beef fillet with mushroom sauce, potatoes and salad Pan fried gurnard with potatoes, cherry tomatoes, and broccoli Let's talk about wait service. We appreciate that hospitality is a hard industry. The pay sucks, the hours suck, there's high turnover, and it's hard to get staff. Excellent service is a rarity, and we don't expect it. But we do hope for service to meet certain basic standards. To be offered another drink when an empty glass is cleared (don't they know that's where the restaurant makes their money?) To be offered dessert at the end of the meal. To be given a steak knife with your steak. For the server to know what is on the menu. For the server to accurately convey your order to the kitchen. Unfortunately, the service at The Shepherds Arms Hotel met none of these hopes. The steak was the best part of the meal. It was a nice piece of meat, well cooked, with a tasty mushroom sauce. The potatoes that came out were roasted, not mashed like we had ordered. That said, they were pretty good, crispy on the outside but slightly underdone. The salad was bad. It was just lettuce and spinach, and the "vinaigrette" was pure oil with a few mustard seeds thrown in. To make matters worse, it wasn't mixed through the leaves adequately so it was all in an oily pool at the bottom. The fish was pretty sad. It was certainly not $36 worth, and it was dry on the outside, although inner moisture was adequate. The hollandaise was flavourless and there wasn't much of it. The broccoli wasn't hot, although we did appreciate it had some char on both sides. It came with a slice of lemon that was at least three years old, bone dry on both cut surfaces. What?! Just cut the edges off you idiots, we would never have known! The whole experience came off as pretty careless. Website

Te Aro, Wellington Halloumi burger Chicken tenders Peri Peri chips Cheesy pita bites We ate dinner here in July 2023 Whoa Nelly, was it smoky in Nando's. We opened the door and walked into a room full of lung clogging smoke and it did not let up the whole time we were there. Later on in the piece the staff opened the door, but that wasn't nearly enough. This was Courtney place Nando's which is quite large, smoking it out was actually a rather impressive feat. Despite the kitchen being on fire, the dining experience was unfortunately not on fire. They encourage you to order with your phone and a QR code at your table. And while that's not a problem in and of itself, the menu on the table doesn't quite marry up with the order of the phone menu, and a few things were just straight up missing. It was clearly just their standard takeaway menu, but rather than saying pickup or delivery you say I'm at table eleven. We don't think it would have taken a lot to switch up the table menus to match the app, or the app to match the tables. And would it have killed them to edit things a little so that dine in customers didn't still have to give their full name, phone number and email. What is that information for? You know where I am, table eleven! Plus, where was the cutlery. We think most people eating sauce covered grilled chicken would take a fork if offered, which we weren't. We did see other tables using cutlery, but we don't know where they got it from. It's also worth noting that some people ordered at the counter while we were there, but the menu instructions specifically tell you to order using the QR code, so that's apparently how they want things to run. Into the food. The cheesy pita was the best of it, hot and soft with a good amount of garlic. The cheese could have been more flavourful and it was a little oily, but still very enjoyable. The chips were dry as hell. We don't mean they needed a sauce, we mean the actual potato in the chips itself was dry. Thank god for the peri peri sprinkle otherwise those chips would've been just plain bad. Speaking of dry, the tenders were next. They hadn't reached the chips level of dryness, but the chicken was unfortunately overdone. The peri peri sauce slathered all over them was okay, we got mild but aren't going to be going out if our way to purchase a bottle The burger was a disappointment. Anytime a halloumi burger is on offer you have our attention. But they'd screwed it up by badly undercooking the

Te Aro, Wellington We ate lunch here in July 2023 Arancini balls Fried chicken Bread with dips Braised beef in butternut bread Whistling Sisters serves their meals tapas style - food comes out whenever its ready, and its made for sharing, which we love. We definitely looked down on our neighbouring table who ordered one plate each and absolutely refused to share, even though two of the dudes had bought large charcuterie platters. Weird. We ordered our four dishes off the main menu, which had ample choice. However we were disappointed to later learn by watching another table be seated that there were two other menus (one brunch and a special one for Matariki) that our waitress didn't even offer us. For shame! The food was mostly good. The bread was fresh and warm with pleasant hummus and a mustardy as dipping sauce. The braised beef in butternut bread is really a taco, which was unexpected but yummy. As a single taco in a thick shell, it was a little hard to share. The chicken wings were an entire wing, from shoulder to phalanx. Practically, this was a bit of a problem. They were very liberally sauced, so pulling apart the wing to eat it was one of our messiest experiences to date. The chicken itself was lovely and moist, with crispy skin, and the sauce had great flavour. The arancini was the worst offering. It had done everything right - good presentation, crispy, nice texture on the rice without clagginess - except it was practically flavourless. According to the menu the flavours were capsicum, parmesan and squid ink with a wasabi mayo. In reality, you could see but not taste the squid ink, the capsicum was a single micro-sliver that was really a garnish atop the ball, the parmesan was barely detectable, and the wasabi mayo completely non-wasabi. Website

Te Aro, Wellington Falafel kebab on rice (this is an iskender) Lamb on kumara chips While it is possible to dine in at Kebabs on Queen, and they don't frown on it, even providing a bin and disposable cutlery, we wouldn't say they were encouraging dine in. On a cold Wellington night the double doors were propped wide open, beckoning the steady flow of drunk kebab shufflers. Also, the stools were too short for the bench by the window. The place was staffed by just one depressed guy. While he was getting away with this at the time we went in, it would only take a few more customers before he would be overwhelmed. The iskender, or kebab on rice as they call it for some reason, was pretty good. The rice was sticky, plenty of sauce, reasonable falafel, and fresh salads in a good ratio. And no godawful big chunks of red onion. The kumara chips aren't great for meat on chips. It felt like a bit of a novelty, maybe a trap for people who are sick of the usual meat on potato chips. While the kumara chips themselves were pretty good, they have a distinct flavour which just doesn't work as meat on chips. Regular potato chips would have been better. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in July 2023 Beef brisket nachos Fish tacos Let's talk in-restaurant movies. We're certainly not against the idea, you'll recall how pleased we were to see Space Jam at Burger Liquor. Tequila Joe's was playing an illegal download of Django Unchained complete with FOR YOUR CONSIDERATION intermittently at the bottom of the screen. That movie is dope and we've seen it multiple times. But for a restaurant? There is gory violence, nudity, and torture. They did play it in black and white which helped tone it down, but still, it was a surprise. At least you couldn't hear the audio. The place was packed (Django Unchained is a popular movie after all) and we were lucky to get a table. The staff were really nice, but weren't very organised. There were four staff whom we observed with increasing scrutiny the longer we waited for our meals. It was a shemozzle, they seemed to lack defined jobs, there was a lot of double handling, and overall they seemed flustered and without purposeful direction. They were doing a steady takeaway trade which slowed down an already slow kitchen so we ended up waiting 45 minutes for our meal. When the food arrived, it was worth the wait. The fish tacos were simple with fresh flavours, crispy battered fish, and we liked how they'd seared the taco shells. The beef nachos were also really nice. We were surprised that the brisket came as big chunks as this was pretty awkward to load onto the corn chips. But the flavours were really good, we liked the liquidy queso in particular. Bookings recommended. Website

Thorndon, Wellington We ate dinner here in August 2023 Degustation Hillside Kitchen is all about locally grown this, sustainable that, organic the other. That's all well and good, as long as the food delivers. And oh boy, did it deliver. This was a 10 course vegetarian degustation, and absolutely everything was made with great care, skill, and a little bit of style. The ingredients were unusual to say the least. Every dish had at least one ingredient we'd never heard of, including a lot of NZ native produce. They managed to turn some of our least favourite vegetables into standout dishes, which we feel is the mark of a truly great restaurant.

column8: 134 High Street, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010
column13: Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in August 2023 Macaroni cheese burger Chicken bites on curly fries After an evening movie, it was 9.30 on a Wednesday when we went looking for a place to eat. After a couple of places had closed kitchens, we had some concerns. Luckily Romans Kitchen, with a menu appealing to the late night stoner crowd, was still pumping. Not pumping for dine-in, which seems to be a throwaway part of their business, but pumping for Uber eats certainly. Everybody loves fatty fried food, but it's surprisingly hard to serve a good, let alone a great, meal of it. Pauly's Diner is a shining beacon showing that it can be done, but most fried eateries are poor to middling. Romans Kitchen falls into this category. The chicken bites were a bit dry, and the sauce combination atop (mayo and tomato) was uninspired. Curly fries are a bad choice of bedding for chicken bites. It was very difficult (especially with the plastic forks provided) to get a forkful of chicken and potato together, with the curly fries spronging away and breaking under fork pressure. Getting curlies instead of regular fries was an "upgrade" for which we paid a premium, but regular chips would have been better. The macaroni cheese burger was not good. Despite not mentioning chicken on the menu description, this is a chicken burger with a layer of macaroni cheese, not a macaroni cheese burger. The firmness of the chicken causes all the macaroni just to squish out everywhere when you bite into it, and it was falling apart left right and centre. Add to this the fact that the flavours were nothing special and you come to the conclusion that this burger was not worth the effort.

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in August 2023 Beef nachos Halloumi burger with chips Anywhere that switches songs halfway through the solo in Hotel California had an uphill climb to impress Business Andy and The Fee-Rex. The Residences decidedly unremarkable meals did nothing to sway our opinion. Perhaps we are being a bit harsh, after all The Residence is a bar first and foremost. Their priority is selling a lot of drinks, playing loud music (up to the good bit at least) and offering fried food that is quick and easy to cook, and that you can eat with your hands. They managed above average in burger construction, and we approved of the shredded lettuce and the onion jam. On the whole, the burger was reasonable. Special shout out to the legend in the kitchen that put way more halloumi in there then we expected. We can't dress up the nachos, they just sucked. All the elements were there, they just messed them all up. Broken chips, flavourless beef mince, awful salsa and guacamole, and nowhere near enough of either. And what's more, the dish itself was too small for what we paid. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate lunch here in August 2023 Roast vegetable wrap Lemongrass & tofu ramen Orient is an importer and distributor of Asian ceramics. If you went by their website, you'd think that's all they do. But they also run a side hustle of a small cafe. It's only 5 tables nestled into their store, so cross your fingers you get a seat. Places jamming in an eatery as an added extra isn't always a good thing, as we experienced just last night. But the food at Orient was so good, they could do it as their sole venture. The roast vegetable wrap was the true hero. We are still reeling. The vegetables were roasted to perfection, dressed in a super tasty sauce and had plenty of seeds for crunch. Then the wrap, oh, the wrap. Begone, bland flatbread. This wrap was a pan fried roti and it was spectacular. Despite being reheated from the cabinet you'd swear it was made fresh. Excellent. The ramen was also strong, especially for a vegan offering. In our experience, it's hard to do a good vegetarian ramen, let alone a vegan one. It was lovely and hearty with great broth. And both meals were pretty good value for money, especially for a central city location. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in October 2023 Steak, eggs and chips Jackfruit burger with chips and aioli The best part about our experience at Jack Hackett's was undoubtedly the live music. We are certainly not always fans of live music in bars/restaurants. Sometimes the music is just plain bad, at other times they're just oppressively loud, and sometimes it just doesn't work. But this was spot on. Music volume very clearly audible but you could still hold a conversation, she had a great voice, and the songs were familiar bangers all the way down (except Heart of Glass, sorry not sorry, Blondie). The food wasn't on par with the music. We made the very traditional order of steak, eggs and chips as it was $20 steak Wednesdays and we love a bargain. The cook on the steak was as we had requested, and the quality of the meat was reasonable for that cut. The eggs were a bit underdone with some raw albumin glooping about. The chips were mediocre and came with a watery aioli. The jackfruit burger had highs and lows. The jackfruit itself was great, juicy and flavourful, somebody could trick you into thinking it was pulled meat. The coleslaw in the burger was neutral, not offensive but not notably good. The BBQ sauce was similarly mediocre. The bun was insanely dry, just a cheap hamburger bun that was past its best by date.

Waiouru We ate lunch here in October 2023 Polenta chips Chicken burger Roast vegetable salad Rustic Eating House is pretty pleased with itself. They are very excited about being a quality restaurant on the side of SH1 where you wouldn't expect to find such a place. A while they're not bad by any stretch, they aren't quite living up to their own hype. The polenta chips themselves were hot and fresh but a bit thinner than ideal. They came with an excellent sauce - a lemony aioli with pesto in it. The chicken burger was quite special, it was a bit spicy and had some interesting seasoning going on. The chips were chunky and well sized. The roast vegetable salad was a disappointment. The vegetables were all cooked, but not well coloured or crispy, and it just didn't have a lot going, although we appreciate the addition of seeds. A note on the Rustic Eating House (Waiouru) versus the Rustic Steak House (Taihape). They are part of the same group, having different but overlapping menus and refer to themselves as 'brother' restaurants. As such, we've reviewed them separately. Website

Taihape We ate lunch here in October 2023 Steak and pepper pie Potato stuffed sausage Banana and cream pancake What a pleasant surprise this place was. We've been burned at cafes that look just like this in the past, with the hot and cold cabinets, the trays, the sterile seating area, and the often telling emptiness. Taihape Bakery & Cafe bucks this trend though, with very good food, although the ambiance could stand to be improved. The steak and pepper pie was just a great pie, great pastry, a lovely meat filling, and a warm peppery flavour that was hot, but not too hot. The potato stuffed sausage did let them down a bit though, had this been a more interesting sausage, and had they seasoned the mash, it could have been a success. And finally the banana and cream pancake was just a fluffy delight. It was full of whipped cream, slices of banana, and a little bit of jam, it really put a smile on Business Andy's dial. A bit of a diamond in the rough, this one. Taihape Bakery & Cafe has no website.

column8: NZ, 88 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011
column13: Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in October 2023 Mushroom broth hot pot Chicken skewers Pork skewers Beef meatballs Fried dumplings We are new to Hot Pot dining so Top Kitchen was a bit exciting for us and had an opportunity to set a bar to meet. Turns out, the bar isn't very high. It wasn't all bad - the broth was very nice, so was the chicken, and the homemade chilli and satay sauces were great. The dumplings were middling, and they offered no selection beyond fried versus steamed. We assume what we got was pork, and that's supported by the gristle, but who really knows. Speaking of gristle, Jesus were the meatballs bad. Worst meat we've had in some time. Not only were they gristly, the flavour was vile. How old were they? And they texture was slimy and rubbery. Bleugh. Website

column8: 1 Hagley Street, Porirua City Centre, Porirua 5022
column13: Porirua We ate dinner here in November 2023 Orange steak Satay hot plate with beef Rice Delusions of grandeur; the restaurant. They had the checklist of things that made you fancy, and boy howdy they checked every single one off it. Tasteless chandelier, check, smooth jazz playing, check, "leather" seats, check. Top Taste serves a mish-mash of Asian cuisines, with Chinese, Korean, Singaporean and Malaysian all featuring on the menu. This is generally a red flag for someone just trying to cherry pick the dishes from each culture that most appeal to kiwi tastes. The satay hot plate was not enjoyable. It was generic sauce satay, not peanut satay, so basically just brown meat sauce. The meat was neither chewy nor gristly, but it had only reached the bare minimum for acceptability. The vegetables were raw across both dishes. At least there was plenty of sauce, enough for our large bowl of rice. Then again, for twelve dollars, we expect a large amount of rice. White rice is one of the cheapest foods known to man, and this had just been scraped straight from the rice cooker, with those hard bits from the sides and everything. For twelve bucks, could you do us the courtesy of fluffing up the rice? Right at the other end of the spectrum, the orange steak was outstanding. When we read orange steak, we scoffed. This meal is normally called orange beef, and we thought it was just another example of Top Taste having ideas above their station. We were very wrong. The meat was delicious, thick pieces of reasonable beef, cooked perfectly in a superb sauce. Little bits of orange peel were very welcome, as was the cooked garlic. It was just the raw veggies that let it down from perfection.

Seatoun, Wellington We ate dinner here in November 2023 Beetroot, honey, pecan and basil bruschetta Blue cheese polenta chips with buffalo sauce Pizza: Half vegetariana, half salsiccie We stumbled across Arcimboldi on a cold, windy Wellington night and are sure glad we did. It looks tiny from the outside, but is long and thin with most of the dining area hidden out the back, alongside their garden where we saw staff picking ingredients. The menu is mostly Italian and everything was bellissimo. The bruschetta was innovative and all the flavours worked great together. The Fee-Rex did get a mystery, rock hard item on her piece which was disconcerting but not a deal-breaker. The polenta chips were made with blue cheese, which was a first for us. It would have been nice for the flavour of the blue cheese to be a bit stronger, and the buffalo sauce was perplexing. Not bad, certainly, but not good either. We felt compelled to eat it, but weren't quite sure at the end whether we actually liked the sauce or not. The pizza was marvellous. Firstly, shout out for offering a half-and-half pizza (for a modest fee) - this lets us enjoy two flavours which we really appreciate. Both were excellent. The vegetarian was no throwaway item, as it often is in other restaurants. This vegetarian could stand proudly alongside any of the other pizzas. The salsiccie had pork fennel sausage on it, which is a favourite of Business Andys. The Fee-Rex has been often unimpressed by this and was apprehensive to order it again. But Arcimboldi had the clever idea to put on just crumbled up bits of sausage meat, rather than slices of sausage. This was a huge improvement. Website

column8: Kiosk 4/80A Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011
column13: We ate dinner here in December 2023 Truffle fries Cheesy garlic bread Amador is not here for dinner. Their niche is the downtown working crowd. They offer a full menu for breakfast and lunch until 2pm, but after this Amador is really a bar with only snacks available. However, just because they're only serving snacks, doesn't mean the food should be bad. The truffle fries smelled like vomit due to an unfortunate combination of excessive amounts of truffle oil mixed with parmesan cheese. The chips themselves were okay, but the smell was confronting. The cheesy garlic bread was terrible. Their biggest problem was the bread. They'd chosen supermarket style hotdot buns which they'd split horizontally and chucked on some garlic butter and mozzerella then grilled them. They were insanely chewy, a genuine effort to bite through, you need to pull in one direction and move your head in the other direction like a dog with a piece of stewing steak, to get a mouthful. Even aside from the awful texture, the flavour was nothing special and they'd put a rim of balsamic glaze around the edge of the plate which was bringing nothing and ended up on your face and arm. Luckily they did do good espresso martinis. They had 3 different kinds and all of them were delicious in thier own way. It wasn't a particularly inventive cocktail menu, just the classics really, and the white lady was too ginny.

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in January 2024 Malai kofta Paneer jalfrezi Plain naan Naan makhani Rice This place will be closed within 3 months. It has zero street appeal. It's sad inside. It looks like it's only been open for a few weeks and already it was just us and one other table there. They didn't do a single takeaway order the whole time we were dining, nor do they have a website or any affiliation with delivery services that could help their takeaway trade. In other words, they're doomed. And they can't fall back on their food either. The malai kofta barely had any taste at all. The sauce was extremely pale and thin, and the koftas were just mashed potato croquettes they had no nuts or sultanas or anything going on. At least the jalfrezi was okay, it had some flavour and the capsicums were welcome. The plain naan was middling and the naan makhani was a waste of time. We ordered it for some excitement, we didn't know what it was and there was no description on the menu. The waiter described it as being laminated with butter. Our excitement heightened, sounded like a naan croissant! This could be the next big thing, the new cronut! Turns out it tastes exactly the same as a plain naan but it's twice the price and falls apart because of the layers. As a final insult, rice wasn't included with the meal. In our opinion this is a predatory practice that should be stamped out at all costs. Literally nobody wants just a curry without rice, that's crazy, especially for dine-in.
