So don't charge us a regular price for a curry then make us pay $3.50 for a small bowl of rice. This kind of thing just makes you feel like they are trying to squeeze you for every penny. Speaking of, the waiter kept trying to upsell us but very inexpertly. He needs to go to the Tikka Talks School of Indian Cuisine Upselling. He was truly a master of the craft and we still regard him very fondly. Incidentally, his restaurant also closed down, so this place has no chance at all. Spice Paradise has no website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in January 2024 Eye fillet with fries and Cafe de Paris butter Creamy pasta with parmesan Mille feuille with strawberries and sunflower cream Crepes Suzette Concord Bistro is a rip off. They've decided they're fancy, they have cloth napkins and French words on the menu after all, and they've hiked those prices up to high heaven. They had large paper menus, which is okay. But then they left the paper menus intentionally on the table after you order so that you used them as a placemat. What is this, a Pizza Hut (R.I.P. dine in Pizza Hut)? Is there a colouring-in picture and a maze on the back? It was so tacky and incongruent. If I'm paying $52 for a steak and chips, $21 per cocktail and a stunning $28 for a pasta with just cream and parmesan (no meat, no veg, nothing), then please take away your paper tablemat. Perhaps they have shares in the forestry industry, because they also insisted we use paper coasters. Why? The main meals were reasonable. The steak was a nice piece of meat, cooked well, the shoestring fries were crisp and the Cafe de Paris butter was good too. The pasta, while basic, was tasty. The service was good, but the wait for each cocktail was too long. The desserts were terrible. It's about as bad as we've had. The mille feuille was like two crackers stacked with yuck sunflower cream. The strawberries were at least fresh and ripe, but they couldn't save it. The crepe suzette disappointed. It came with a little cast iron frying pan of flaming cointreau, a nice bit of pageantry, but it was just far too much. Once that was in there all you could taste was cointreau, which was not enjoyable. Bookings recommended. Website (this website is an abomination, seriously, who okayed this?)

Calamari with garlic mash and rocket Lamb rack with roast potato Vegetarian saffron rice cake Baklava Boulcott Street Bistro knows service. The maitre d' was a true delight, he made you feel extremely welcome and like family, and while this restaurant is a bit snooty he certainly wasnâ€™t. When our buoyant family party of 11 was leaving, he gave a warm handshake and just seemed thrilled to have met us. He even earned a tip, a very rare occurrence within our family. The bartender was also spot on, friendly and funny, and all the staff were just generally great. The food was pretty good, but hadnâ€™t quite reached greatness. The calamari was a bit pedestrian. Both the lamb rack and rice cake were good meals, but just didnâ€™t knock our socks off. The standout was the baklava which was absolutely delicious especially the lemon creme fraiche on the side, we would be thrilled to have that again. Bookings recommended

column8: The Majestic Centre, Ground Floor/100 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011
column13: Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in March 2024 Tonkotsu Ramen Beef teriyaki Hey Ramen, get some better quality meat. When it comes to a simple dish like ramen, you can't skimp on the quality. Both the beef and pork were insanely dry, to the point we wondered whether the pork hadn't been cooked to order. The non-meat ingredients weren't doing much to pick up the slack. And only one piece of naruto, you tightwads. Website

Pipitea, Wellington We ate dinner here in April 2024 Lamb rump, polenta, broccolini, pistachio & lime gremolata Ribeye, cafe de paris butter, jus, and fries We didn't enjoy our trip to the Thistlle Inn. We stood around for a long time near the bar feeling confused, being completely ignored without so much as a greeting or "be with you shortly". We saw a bar snacks menu on the bar, and we then stumbled upon a proper restaurant menu at the unmanned maitre'd station. Finally we were seated and bought water to our table, but it was sparkling and contained both lemon and cucumber. The Fee-Rex hates sparkling water. She hates water with lemon in it. And she hates water with cucumber in it, so you can imagine how she felt about receiving all 3 in a single glass, unbidden, and with no other option offered. We often order cocktails and then don't talk about them, but tonight they deserve special mention. Not because they were good though. The espresso martini was watery A.F. and was cleared off the table before it was even empty. And we also tried a dessert cocktail featuring coffee and dulce de leche which tasted awful and had to be made twice as the first time they forgot to put any alcohol in it. To make matters worse, we waited a very long time for our meals. When they finally arrived we were far from impressed. The lamb rump was fatty, the polenta, sloppy, and the gremolata was a flavourless non event. It was especially offensive with a $42 price tag. The steak was somehow even worse. We ordered it medium but it came well overdone. It had a marmite-y jus and a deplorable cafe de paris butter that just tasted like plain butter but was bright yellow. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in April 2024 Chicken wings Chipas Loaded fries Calamari Cheese quesdeillas Corn chips with corn and cheese dip Ham and cheese empanada Jalapeno bites Flan with burnt caramel sauce Churros with chocolate sauce If we were just rating service, El Barrio would be a 4. Our waitress was a true delight. Friendly, attentive without being overbearing, alerting us to pertinent cocktail specials, we were big fans. Unfortunately, she was let down by the kitchen. We ordered a sharing platter, which was very hit and miss. The jalapeno bites were good, spicy but not too hot, fresh and flavourful. The flan was well executed, however the 'burnt caramel' sauce was more like 'watered down golden syrup' which was overpowering in flavour compared to the flan. The calamari was also pretty reasonable - often on a sharing platter you're in for some chewy squid, but that wasn't the case here. The highlight was the churros, which were a true victory. Business Andy is quite the churros fan, despite them regularly proving to be disappointing. El Barrio's churros were fluffy and light, unlike the chewy offerings usually available. The chocolate sauce was good and plentiful, although the menu also mentioned a caramel sauce which was absent. Speaking of absent, where were the "marinated green olives" promised in the serving platter. There were a few green mush sauces, perhaps one of these was squished olives, although it didn't seem like it. The loaded fries and quesedilla were also let downs, and the rest of the offerings were middling. We also tried several of their cocktails. If you've got a sweet tooth, try the passionfruit daiquiri. As a final note, while we didn't participate, we did enjoy being offered a free salsa dance class at the end of our meal. El Barrio seemed like they genuinely wanted us to have a good time. Website

Wellington Central, Wellington We ate dinner here in April 2024 Kung pao chicken Orange beef Sometimes, our quest to bring you raw unfettered reviews takes us to grand locations. And other times, it takes us to the cold unforgiving lobby of an apartment building with non stop foot traffic of pizza-carrying residents. We didn't know what to expect when we saw Jeff Cafe. It looked closed, and the name gave us no clues. Turns out Jeff serves Chinese food and is much more popular than one might expect. It's small, being a lobby, and only had 5 tables, but 4 of them were full. We also saw 3 takeaway orders during our dining experience. Why other people were eating at Jeff Cafe we weren't sure, as it clearly wasn't because the food was good. The orange beef, a real favourite of the Fee-Rex, was the worst we've ever had. The meat was clearly ancient, was tough, and very thickly cut. The kung pao chicken was inoffensive but forgettable. We scoffed down our meals then got the hell out of Jeff's frigid ice cave.

column8: Ground Floor Skycity/346 Victoria Street, Hamilton Central, Hamilton 3204
column13: Te Aro, Wellington Orange beef with rice Szechuan lamb with rice Fried dumplings BBQ pork Fried squid Shanghai Restaurant claims to be Wellington's oldest Chinese restaurant, being in service for over 50 years. Their decor supports that - it's proper classic Chinese restaurant stuff, with tablecloths covered with a glass panel, a crowded lobster tank and tacky art on the walls. The food was mostly middling to poor, but we would like to give a shoutout to the orange beef. It was hot, fresh, juicy and flavourful. Inscrutibly it came with a whole head of steamed broccoli which was very unwelcome, but otherwise it was excellent. The rest didn't fare so well. The dumplings were waterproof in texture, which was no use for sauce absorption, and the innards were crumbly. The squid was chewy with floury batter and sad sauce which didn't stick well to the food. The BBQ pork and szechuan lamb were middle of the road. Website

Wellington Central Beef burger and chips Lamb cutlets with cauliflower puree, beetroot, and broccolini Dining out is a discretionary expense, and while there are certain intangibles involved that are hard to put a dollar value on, like not having to clean up after yourself, it's generally clear when you are getting good value for money. Likewise, it's often excruciatingly clear when something is poor value. And while that's definitely not the most important thing when you're eating out, you hope that a restaurant leaves some kind of impact other than "what a ripoff." Whitby didn't give a hoot about value for money. We ordered two cocktails that were almost indistinguishable from one another, however one was priced at $8 more than the other. The burger was more than four Big Mac's worth of dollars, but certainly wasn't more than four Big Mac's worth of trouble. The lamb and its jus were probably the nicest things they served, although there was still some gristle, and the sides that came with it were wankily arranged to disguise that there was bugger all to actually eat. The vegetables were a cauliflower puree, roast beetroot, tepid brocollini and some mystery pale red thing - a yam? A note about service. There were a lot of staff present, 7 visible at once at one point. Yet our burger we ordered without tomato came with tomato. Our plates sat on our table after we finished for far too long. In fact they were still there when we left, what if we'd wanted dessert? And to top it off, when we finally did go to leave, we waited at the hostess stand for an inordinate period with nobody around. It was long enough for the Fee-Rex to take a pen and to rearrange their staples on the counter. Website

Thorndon, Wellington We ate dinner here in June 2024 Cauliflower fritters Lamb ragu Eye fillet with chips Carrots with za'atar Daisy's serves upmarket fare in a cosy atmosphere and is probably upset that she didn't get a 4. While this meal was good, it wasn't quite great. The carrots were a highlight, well cooked with some caramelisation and interesting flavours. The steak was a lovely piece of meat, but was unevenly cooked, ranging from medium to rare depending on your bite. The ragu was tasty, we particularly appreciated the generous topping of parmesan. Call us traditionalists, but we expected the fritters to be flat, a la corn fritter. We were tickled to find these ones were balls. The flavour was odd and controversial. There was tumeric and something citrus-y, and overall the experience wasn't unpleasant, but nor was it something you'd want to order again. Website

Dannevirke We ate dinner here in June 2024 Italian pizza (salami, ham, olives, mushroom, onion) Cheesy jalapeno bites Pizza Castle? Pizza dungeon more like it. Well, maybe that's a bit harsh, it wasn't damp or dark. But it was cold and bad stuff happened here. Beside having seating for 14, Pizza Castle gave no other indication that dine-in was even an option. There was no cutlery, no water, no plates, not a single serviette in sight. We ate from the box. The bites were basically super salty crumbed balls of low-flavour cheese with tiny bits of jalapeno in them along with some unwelcome corn. They were not spicy, nor were they flavourful. They needed a dipping sauce desperately, but there was none on hand. And the pizza had a reasonable base, but the toppings were very bland. Website

Tawa, Wellington Rating: 2 We ate lunch here in June 2024 Beef burger Fish and chips Mocha As we gazed about our surrounds at Chipmunks, we saw what was perhaps the most captive audience that has ever existed. The 'Munk could have been peddling truly abysmal food and they would have still had a steady flow of bored parents and excited children ordering donuts, coffees, and "frogs in ponds" which were criminally overpriced Freddo frogs in cups of green jelly. Fortunately for us, they took the opportunity to aim a little higher than that, and served up a couple of pleasant surprises. The mocha was genuinely good, a pleasant balance between coffee and sweetness, and not too much of either. The ciabatta that enclosed the burger was excellent, fresh and soft, and perfectly toasted. And the chips were hot and fresh, salted just the amount, and had no nasty old oil flavour. The fish was crisp, although we felt the quality of the actual fish was middling. The fish and chips came with what was unfortunately just mixed salad leaves out of a bag with an almost insultingly sparse dribble of balsamic reduction over the top, what a trudge finishing this salad was. That same salad mix found its way into the burger too, but overall, the burger was actually pretty good, and was the highlight. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in July 2024 Cauliflower tacos Chicken burger with chips Dirty Little Secret pumps on a Thursday for drag night bingo, but on a Tuesday at 8pm she was pretty deserted. Nevertheless the bar staff were friendly, but using our bingo winnings (first place, what's up) via their app was a huge pain in the ass. The cauliflower tacos were a rip off. $22 for two tacos, which were small and very basic. Cauliflower, some kind of sauce, and a 'salsa' that was just chopped up tomatoes. $11 worth, we think not. The chicken burger was better. While the bun was on the stale side, the chicken was crispy and flavourful, it held together well and the slaw, pickles and cheese were a lovely combination. The chips were pretty good, and we welcomed the accompanying aioli.

Wellington Central We ate dinner here in August 2024 Pork belly bites Flatbread with hummus Chicken tenders The Green Man had a very small menu. Aside from starters, it had only 4 mains, plus the Wellington On A Plate burger. We made the decision when we moved BAATFR to Wellington that during WOAP we would not be reviewing the burgers. Why? Because WOAP is a special item not usually available and is not necessarily representative of the cuisine or quality of the establishment. Since the menu was so wee and we didn't fancy the sound of the mains we just got a few starters. The pork belly was surprisingly good, and the flatbread was no slouch either. The tenders were anything but tender. Dry, dry, dry like a chicken jerky. We did appreciate the pickled onion and capsicum plus the dipping sauce, but the tender itself was disastrous. We were excited to see three espresso martinis on their menu. We were crushed to hear they were not serving them, nor any cocktails, that night. We received the excuse that they'd had a special on cocktails the night before and had run out of ingredients. This excuse doesn't stand up to inspection. There were a dozen cocktails on that menu. You don't have the ingredients to make any? Yet you can still serve other mixed drinks? That maths ain't mathsin. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in September 2024 Chicken curry with rice Beef brisket with rice Roti Honestly, we wish we could rate it higher based on just the friendliness of the hostess. She was something else, we were just superbly looked after. And the meals came out fast too. However what came out was only passable on the whole. The broth in the chicken curry was absolutely delicious, but the chicken was old and dry. The beef was practically offensive. It wasn't brisket for a start, but was the oldest, cheapest beef in the city instead, with plenty of gristle. And unlike the chicken curry, the beef broth didn't save that meal. Roti is often an easy win, but for some reason this roti was really dry, crispy almost, with insufficient lamination. And we somehow ordered two plates of the stuff. Oh well. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in September 2024 Cheese quesedilla Cheesy gordita crunch Beef nachos Churros The Beast is slain at last. The spectre of Taco Bell on Cuba has haunted us forever. Ever since we first saw him sitting there on his throne of skulls right beside the bus stop. No more. And just like Subway, a great weight was lifted from our shoulders as we ticked this chain off the list. It turns out that we'd been building Taco Bell up in our minds like some kind of final boss of fast food for far too long. The overall impression is that it's just bland. The quesadilla only escaped being as bland as the rest of the dishes by the included sauce sachets. Neither of which was fantastic, but at least they added something. The nachos of the loaded nachos came with some kind of red dust scattered all over them, but alas, all you couldn't taste it at all. Likewise the beef mince was flavourless, and the cheese sauce, barely detectable. At least the guac tasted somewhat like avocado, but is it really made from avocados? The gordita fared mostly the same, it had the same bland mince, but also had some kind of sauce in it that the Fee-Rex really didn't appreciate. We did actually like the texture, with a crunchy taco shell inside soft flat bread. The churros were the only thing we'd have again. They were soft and fluffy on the inside, crunchy on the outside, and absolutely smothered in a tasty mix of cinnamon and sugar. Their chocolate sauce was thin, but there was a lot of it, no sad rationing required. A note on value. The menu at Taco Bell looks really cheap, with dishes half to two thirds of the cost you'd expect if ordering them somewhere else. Don't be fooled. Aside from the difference in quality, there is a substantial size difference. Many cafe nachos are so big we struggle for finish them. After we ate the above meal, we came home and had toast. Website

Te Aro, Wellington Mozzarella sticks with spicy honey Toscana pizza - Italian sausage, mushroom, scamorza, sweet onion Baked cheesecake with blackberries Scopa Pizzeria is a popular place. We've clocked it before when in the area and noticed its fullness. Tonight when we showed up, as usual reservation-less to a heaving establishment, we were told we could wait for a table. We weren't the only ones waiting, but the food service was pretty fast and we only had to do about 15 minutes standing around at the bar before being seated. We took that time to have cocktails (the bottled marg and the bottled cherry concoction) which unfortunately we can't recommend. But we can recommend the mozzarella sticks and the pizza, which were both excellent, especially the cheese sticks and the delicious hot honey. In case you're wondering, as we were, hot honey means both spicy and warm. And while we do appreciate a nice baked cheesecake, this one fell a bit short. It was sunken in the middle, too cold, and the coulis that came with it was far too full of seeds. Bookings strongly recommended.

Waiouru We ate lunch here in October 2024 Battered fish Chips Fried chicken Carrot cake Fast Lane Restaurant caters to the passing-through-Waiouru-wanna-stop-for-less-than-five-minutes crowd, right next to the public rest rooms where the off-brand air blade hand dryers emitted a strangely unpleasant odour. Fast Lane Restaurant offers various fried foods in a warmer, a chilled cabinet of sandwiches and cakes, as well as a fish and chips shop style cooked menu. It was a long weekend and Fast Lane was doing steady trade. Despite this, the chips tasted like they'd been in the warmer for quite some time. They were soft, floury, and stale - a sobering reminder that while most chips are fairly similar and rather enjoyable, it is certainly possible for them to be bad. The fish looked appealing externally but was very fishy in flavour. The fried chicken fared a bit better. It had a crispy coating but was pretty oily and bland. The carrot cake was the best item but even that was merely passable. The decor was extremely dated and shabby, napkins and wooden cutlery hard to come by, and we inexplicably selected the table next to three grotty open bins. We recommend avoiding the Fast Lane - switch to the slow lane, wait an extra five minutes and get some food you might actually want to eat. Website

Te Aro, Wellington We ate dinner here in November 2024 Onion rings Pulled pork loaded fries Falafel Popcorn chicken Mushroom arancini Woah. Best onion rings ever. Literally the best onion rings we have ever had. You know how sometimes you want to order onion rings, then you hesitate because you've been burned one too many times by compound extruded onion ring BS. You can put your fears aside at The Tasting Room. Fresh. Piping hot. Homemade. Actual rings of onion. Big. Crispy yet also a little squishy. You can have all these things. But it's not over yet because let us tell you about the sauce. "Chip shop curry sauce" was the title. We want to go to that chip shop. It was curry-ish, but not over spicy but it had a wonderfully warm flavour, there was tonnes of it, and it sure did pair well with the onion. And yes, we dipped everything else in it too. Leave no curry sauce behind. After those heights it's hard for the other dishes to measure up, and they didn't. Worst of all was the popcorn chicken, which was dry and not very flavourful. The arancini was also on the dry side, but not bad. The falafel and loaded fries were also fine, but nothing to write home about. Unlike the sonnet we've just composed about the onion rings. Website

Thorndon, Wellington We ate dinner here in November 2024 Orange beef Thai style eggplant with pork Perhaps it's partly our fault for trying to have dinner during the peak office-do weeks, but what a schemozzle. They were just not set up for a big table of drunken revellers to be whooping and hollering in the back. The other, much more demure large table beside them was quite upset to be seated beside such a rowdy group, but we had a great time just people watching. We certainly had a lot of time to fill. Despite all the other tables already being served by the time we had finished ordering, we still had to wait about 30 minutes for our dinner. How are you so slow, especially for Chinese food which is usually lightning quick? Yes, there was an adjoining takeaway wing, but gauged by the level of traffic coming in and out of there it wasn't particularly busy. The orange beef, which is Fee-Rex's favourite, was underwhelming to say the least. There was no orange flavour and the beef pieces were large and super chewy. The eggplant dish was quite interesting. You may think that it would be pieces of fried eggplant, and pieces of fried pork. But you'd be wrong. They had somehow combined the pork and the eggplant together (poking the pieces of pork into the eggplant perhaps?), battered and fried it as one large unit. Then it had been placed in a sauce, which was a bit too sweet and a bit too salty, but the overall effect was surprising and unexpected. Unfortunately this wasn't enough to compensate for the bad beef, long wait and poor ambiance. Website

Levin We ate lunch here in December 2024 Pulled pork tostadas Mushrooms on toastÂ In the heavy northbound Christmas traffic, we decided to pull in at the first place we saw in Levin. Despite only being 12.30, it wasnâ€™t clear on entering the Firebird whether it was open or not. There was one member of staff, who hadnâ€™t turned around to face us, and a couple of people sitting in this large, slightly dark room with a second-hand-shop vibe. We were informed that they were open, but that there were no pizzas, nothing from the mains menu, and actually she would prefer we just ordered from the brunch menu. This narrowed it down to about six options.Â Firebird has a Mexican slant to their menu, and we were looking forward to the tostadas. Yet another unavailable item, she didnâ€™t have any of their usual tostada bases but popped everything on a big tortilla instead. It was pretty good but not groundbreaking.Â What was groundbreaking was the mushrooms on toast. The seasoning was incredible - we couldnâ€™t name exactly what was going on and reckon some of the Mexican spices had snuck in there, but it was a flavour explosion. This kind of dish reminds you that mushrooms on toast, so often a throwaway, can be a total powerhouse when done correctly.Â Website

Whanganui We ate lunch here in December 2024Â Pancakes with maple syrup, strawberry and cream Vegetable focacciaÂ On a sunny December 27th, Windermere Berry Farm is exactly as packed as you would expect. Despite this, everything came out really fast. The vegetable focaccia was bloody good, and that is far from a given. Many veg sandwiches are thoughtless throwaways with mismatched innards, but this focaccia had been given some thought. The caramelised onion, pesto, mushroom and spinach all worked together perfectly and we would be happy to enjoy it again anytime.Â Same goes for the pancakes. They were big and fluffy with tonnes of strawberries. Really, really good strawberries too. Sometimes places use their D-grade fruit in settings like this, but these strawberries could happily be eaten alone. Our only complaint would be that there wasnâ€™t enough syrup - fluffy pancakes are like a sponge so you really need to drench them in the maple.Â Websites

column8: 63 George Street, Palmerston North Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate dinner here in January 2025Â Malai kofta Â Plain naan Garlic naan Onion bhaji On New Years Day in Palmerston North, dining options were limited. Our first two places we randomised were closed, and we then drove the streets looking for bright lights. We werenâ€™t the only people to have found Indian Indulgence, with 5 other tables plus some people getting takeaways. Despite this the service was prompt and friendly.Â The onion bhaji was acceptable. It looked like it had promise, it was at least individual bits of fried onion rather than those big gross onion cakes with the floury bits that you sometimes get. And the tamarind sauce was a good consistency, sometimes they can be too thin.Â Naan wise there was a high high and a low low. The plain naan was too thin and crisp, it wasnâ€™t a poppadom but it was thinking about it. On the other hand, the garlic naan was quite exceptional. The Fee-Rex doesnâ€™t usually rate garlic naan, believing them often to be an added expense for no added flavour. But this one was soft and super garlicky with a bit of herbs on there too, so different to the plain naan you wouldnâ€™t think theyâ€™d been made by the same person.Â We are in a transition period from mild to medium curry. After years of eating mild curries we have been finding a lot of unpleasant sweetness, so we are experimenting with going medium. However, this can make it a little harder to judge our familiar favourites as they donâ€™t taste like we are used to. Overall, the sauce was good but not great. The koftas were pretty plain but at least were nice and soft as opposed to rubbery.Â Website

column8: Down Town Food Court Shop 6/60 Broadway Avenue, Central, Palmerston North 4410
column13: Palmerston North We ate lunch here in January 2025Â Bicol Express Quesadilla with chipsÂ King Cafe is apparently a â€˜Filipino-Kiwi Kitchenâ€™, but you wouldnâ€™t necessarily know it to look at the menu. There were several Mexican dishes, a bunch of fried basics (think tenders, loaded fries etc), spaghetti, and what they bragged was a very messy cheeseburger. Also, and forgive our lack of culture here, we hadnâ€™t realised that tiny frozen mixed veg was such a Filipino staple. We saw a meal coming out with an absolute mountain on the stuff on the side of the plate, which caused us to be very wary in our ordering.Â The quesadilla was passable. They hadnâ€™t described what was in the quesadilla, simply labelling it â€˜quesadillaâ€™ and allowing ones imagination to wander. Turns out it was chicken, with a tomato-BBQ-esque sauce, cheese, and of course some frozen mixed veg, although thankfully not much, you wouldnâ€™t have known it was there if you couldnâ€™t see the peas randomly rolling out of it. The accompanying fries were pretty good, kudos on the chicken salt, and they were helpful for mopping up all the quesadilla innards that spilled everywhere.Â The pork dish was, per the menu description, spicy, although not unpleasantly so. Actually, the flavour was quite nice. There was thankfully no frozen mixed veg, but the pork was of a very poor quality. The prawn crackers were a welcome addition, and there was a side salad that had a reasonable dressing.Â All in all, reasonable. Website

Tawa, Wellington Red curry with kumara and pineapple Drunken noodles with beef Chicken satay skewers How many pieces of pineapple would you expect to have in a kumara and pineapple curry? 5? 6? If you answered zero, you are either the proprietors of Thai Country Cafe, or a psychopath. Making matters worse, we're not 100% sure there was any kumara in it either. There was certainly a starchy vegetable, but it was either very pale kumara, or just potato. Either way, damning. Fortunately for the proprietors of Thai Country Cafe, the drunken noodles were pretty reasonable. There was a good amount of kick, plenty of Thai basil, the beef was acceptable, and everything they said was going to be in there was present. In retrospect, we were stupid to buy the skewers, and by we, we mean mostly Business Andy. Not only do we not need that much food, but it's such a fraught menu item. They are so often dry like they were tonight, and the meat always comes off the skewer itself very poorly, causing you to either deepthroat the whole pointy thing, or rip it off with your hands like some kind of animal.

column8: shop 4/383 Andersons Bay Road, South Dunedin, Dunedin 9012
column13: Newtown, Wellington Fries Onion rings BBQ double toastie Tandoori bites Tandoori burger Mash n Gravy Chicking, remove your crown, you are being dethroned. You can't give us food like that and expect to still occupy the throne. Beyond the food, the ambiance was abysmal. The place was filthy - we arrived at 5.30, the place was not busy yet somehow the tables were covered in crumbs and the floor was covered in debris including two white feathers - we'd be concerned but after eating that meal there's no way the chicken was that fresh. The table had been pushed so it had made holes in the filthy wall. There were plenty of flies to boot. If the place was empty, how come we had to wait 15-20 minutes and the food wasn't even fresh? In the time we were waiting they served 2 or 3 takeaway customers, but they were far from busy and had four visible members of staff. The chips were old as the hills, and the popcorn chicken was older than the hills. The burger was luke warm, but at least the chicken inside was fresh. The tandoori bites were also fresh, but the outside was floppy rather than crispy. The BBQ double toastie was a tonne of meat, real heart attack stuff, but was one of the less offensive items overall. The clear winner was the mash, which we would have again (better than KFC). Shame it didn't come with a spoon, so you only had the option to dip your flaccid chips into it. Easily the most offensive item was the onion rings. For a start, $6.50 was their standard price for 6 onion rings. As we were purchasing with other items, we earned the "hot steal" deal, 6 for $5. The picture on the menu showed beer battered, happy looking rings. What we got was big, sweet, sad, stale composite onion rings worth 20c at best.
